data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：电吉他失真的性质、应用及其在音乐中的角色

不同观点：
• Tade0认为电吉他的失真波形通常是锯齿波，只有在琴弦正中拨动时才会接近三角波。他还提到失真的音色受演奏技巧影响，例如拨弦方向，并举例像Mesa Boogie这样的放大器通过利用有限的增益带宽积（GBP）来获得特定的音色。此外，他指出像BOSS DS-1的效果器，新版芯片虽然技术上更优，但因缺少老版芯片的特性而失去了独特的音色。

• Kazinator指出单音失真因电路改进迅速被主流接受，但难听的失真仍被排斥。他认为失真音色丰富，与弓弦乐器和木管乐器有相似之处。尽管有些前卫音乐人会使用难听的失真音色，但这些音色仍属小众。他还讨论了失真音色在复杂和声部分的局限性，并以爵士/摇滚融合为例，说明失真在独奏中的接受度高于和声部分。此外，他强调重金属音乐依赖大量失真，并通过复杂节奏和分层录音创造独特的音色纹理。

• Myself248分享了一个个人理论，认为失真吉他音色类似于发动机声音，象征自由。他通过播放Pink Floyd的音乐让妹妹理解失真的音色。

• Drops引用Brian Eno的话，认为失真是媒介突破极限的标志，许多现代艺术正是通过这些“失败”的音色表达极致的情感与事件。

• Driggs赞赏作者对失真的详细分析，但认为其写作风格过于学术化。他推荐了一段Henry Rollins和Don Was关于失真的对话，认为更具艺术性。

补充讨论：
• 失真音色的技术细节，如波形、增益带宽积对音色的影响。
• 失真音色在不同音乐类型中的应用与接受度，特别是重金属和爵士/摇滚融合。
• 失真作为艺术表达的一部分，其文化和情感意义。
• 学术性讨论与艺术性表达之间的平衡。

data.title: German conservatives sound alarm over gold reserves held in US
data.author: anigbrowl
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了德国对存放在美国纽约联邦储备银行的黄金储备安全性的担忧。由于美国政治局势不稳定，包括总统特朗普的干预行为和对司法系统的挑战，一些德国政客开始质疑这些黄金是否仍然安全。早在2012年，德国议员Marco Wanderwitz就曾要求检查这些黄金，但未成功。如今，随着美国政治不确定性增加，他再次提出这一问题。欧盟议员Markus Ferber也呼吁对存放在美国的德国黄金进行更多检查。尽管德国央行行长Joachim Nagel表示信任美联储，但过去曾有右翼民粹主义者推动类似检查，导致部分黄金被运回德国。这反映了德国对黄金储备安全的持续关注。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：数字资产的所有权与控制权

不同观点：
• 观点一：数字资产应由用户完全控制。skylurk认为，如果数字资产（如加密货币或NFT）不由用户自己掌控（即私钥或钱包不在用户手中），那么这些资产就不真正属于用户。他引用了传统说法“Not your keys, not your coins”来支持自己的立场，强调去中心化和个人主权的重要性。
  
• 观点二：托管服务有其存在的必要性。一些用户认为，托管服务（如交易所或第三方钱包）为新手或不愿管理自己私钥的用户提供了便利和安全性。这些服务可以降低用户因自身操作失误而导致的资产丢失风险，并且在某些情况下提供保险或赔偿措施。

• 观点三：用户责任与安全意识的平衡。部分讨论者认为，虽然用户应该尽量掌握自己资产的控制权，但现实情况是，很多用户缺乏必要的技术知识或安全意识，容易因操作不当导致资产损失。因此，他们认为在教育用户提高安全意识和使用托管服务之间应该有一个平衡。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于"去中心化"理想与现实操作难度之间的矛盾。一些用户坚持完全去中心化的理念，认为这是区块链技术的核心价值，而另一些用户则关注实际操作中的安全性和便利性。
• 技术门槛问题：一些讨论者提到，私钥管理对于非技术用户来说过于复杂，这是阻碍更多人进入区块链领域的一个重要因素。
• 责任归属问题：如果用户选择使用托管服务并丢失资产，责任应该归属于用户自己还是托管方，这也是讨论中的一个关键点。

Can the United States be trusted with Germany’s gold?
Its leader is trying to
cripple
the country’s most important industry. His deputy thinks it’s a
pathetic freeloader
. The man who has their ear is throwing what look a lot like Nazi salutes and openly
interfering in its elections
to support a far-right party that its own intelligence service thinks is a
threat to the constitution
.
No wonder, then, that some politicians in Germany are worried that what was for decades seen as one of the world’s most reliable storehouses might not be so secure after all.
Advertisement
Advertisement
Germany holds the world’s second-largest gold reserves, and keeps 37 percent of them — some 1,236 metric tons, worth €113 billion — in the vaults of the New York Federal Reserve. Those holdings of precious metal guarantee that, should the need ever arise, the Bundesbank has access to something it can change into U.S. dollars (or any other hard currency).
The very idea that they might not be safe would have been considered ridiculous from 1945 ... until a couple of weeks ago. But the certainties of Germany’s postwar existence have been turned on their head and — as the recent
scrapping
of a notorious cap on public borrowing showed — the unthinkable is suddenly very thinkable indeed. All the more so given evidence of U.S. President Donald Trump’s willingness to push the limits of his powers and assert presidential primacy over the
judicial system
.
German tabloid Bild, owned by POLITICO parent company Axel Springer,
reported
on Thursday that outgoing Christian Democratic Union (CDU) lawmaker Marco Wanderwitz is one of those concerned.
Already in 2012, Wanderwitz had unsuccessfully requested to inspect the gold holdings as part of an effort to pressure the bank to either take a more active role as a custodian, or to repatriate it to Germany.
“Of course, the question now arises again,” Wanderwitz said in comments reported by Bild.
European Union lawmaker Markus Ferber, also of the CDU, equally called for more checks on German gold stored in the U.S.
Advertisement
Advertisement
“Official representatives of the Bundesbank must personally count the bars and document their results,” Bild quoted him as saying.
In the past, the idea that gold stored in official vaults may not be safe has generally been the preserve of cranks and conspiracy theorists. However, it has been revived, ironically, by none other than the billionaire and
éminence grise
of the Trump administration, Elon Musk, who has
called
for an inspection of the U.S.’s own gold reserves.
You do not talk about Bullion Club
For the Deutsche Bundesbank, which is tasked with the safe management of Germany’s most valuable financial asset, the first rule of Bullion Club is you do not talk about Bullion Club, and you most certainly don’t cast aspersions on fellow members.
“We have a trustworthy and reliable partner in the Fed in New York for the storage of our gold holdings,” said Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel during a February press conference, a comment that the bank directed POLITICO back to on Friday. “It does not keep me awake at night. I have complete confidence in our colleagues at the American central bank.”
“We have a trustworthy and reliable partner in the Fed in New York for the storage of our gold holdings,” said Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel | Kirill Kudryavtsev/AFP via Getty Images
However, it’s barely a decade since the Bundesbank was jolted into similar action, when the more immediate public concern was that Germany’s accumulated wealth would be frittered away bailing out the rest of the eurozone.
In 2013, a noisy campaign driven by right-wing populists — which resonated enough with the broader population to embarrass then-Chancellor Angela Merkel — led to the Bundesbank repatriating all of the gold it had previously stored in the Bank of France’s vaults.  At the time, the Bundesbank argued that it no longer needed a means to access foreign currency in Paris, now that Germany and France shared the euro.
Today, over half of the Bundesbank’s reserves are stored on its premises in Frankfurt. Outside the U.S., the remaining 13 percent is held at the Bank of England.

data.article_summary: 文章主要讲述了2025年美国高等教育面临的困境，尤其是在第二次特朗普政府执政下，大学成为针对目标。政府对多样性、公平性和包容性项目展开调查，削减联邦资金，并试图驱逐参与亲巴勒斯坦活动的国际学生。哥伦比亚大学被迫同意政府的多项要求以恢复资金，随后校长辞职。在这种趋势下，许多高校领导者选择谨慎行事，但韦斯利安大学校长迈克尔·罗斯则公开反对政府干预，支持大学应坚持原则。罗斯在处理校内抗议和外部压力时，强调自由言论和参与公共事务的重要性，并批评其他大学以中立为借口避免麻烦。文章还提到罗斯对2024年大选前高校不愿公开支持非党派活动的失望。总体而言，文章反映了当前美国高校在政治压力下的复杂处境和罗斯的坚定立场。

Last Friday could have passed for a lovely spring day on the Connecticut campus of Wesleyan University. Students with books and laptops dotted a green hillside; flocks of admissions visitors trailed tour guides; baseball season had just begun, and practice was under way. It was almost possible to forget the grim straits of American higher education in 2025.
Colleges and universities have been early targets of the second Trump Administration. In the past month, the Administration has announced it will investigate diversity, equity, and inclusion efforts at more than fifty schools; cut hundreds of millions of dollars in federal funding from such institutions as Johns Hopkins and the University of Pennsylvania; and sought to deport international students involved in pro-Palestinian activism. Columbia received a letter from the federal government issuing demands—which included making changes to discipline and admission policies, and placing the department of Middle East, South Asian, and African Studies under “academic receivership”—to be met as a “precondition” for negotiating the restoration of four hundred million dollars in federal funding. The university agreed to these demands the following week; the week after that, the university’s president resigned.
Columbia’s capitulation was in line with a general trend toward circumspection. The memory of Congress grilling university presidents in 2023 seems to be fresh among leaders in higher ed: few want to risk either their jobs or their budgets by saying the wrong thing. A handful of exceptions have stood out; for example, President Christopher Eisgruber, of Princeton, who wrote a piece for
The Atlantic
about “
The Cost of the Government’s Attack on Columbia
.” (This week, the Administration suspended dozens of grants to Princeton.) But perhaps none has been as voluble or persistent as Michael Roth, who has been president of Wesleyan since 2007.
Roth is a historian and a Wesleyan alumnus who, as an undergraduate, designed a major in the history of psychological theory. His scholarship has dealt with Freud and memory but also colleges as institutions, in books such as “
Safe Enough Spaces
” (2019) and “
The Student: A Short History
” (2023). Recent years have brought an increasingly political thrust to both his writing (for national media and his
presidential blog
) and to his work as president. In 2023, in response to the Supreme Court’s ruling against affirmative action, Wesleyan ended legacy admissions.
When Wesleyan students joined the national wave of protests over the war on Gaza, Roth—who describes himself as a supporter of both free speech and Israel’s right to exist—tangled with student protesters as well as with those who wanted him to shut the protests down. Meanwhile, in interviews and essays, he took administrators at other colleges to task for embracing the principles like those found in the “
Kalven report
”—a 1967 document out of the University of Chicago, which advanced the argument that universities should almost always remain scrupulously neutral. (Such stances were, he told me, “a cover for trying to stay out of trouble.”) As the Trump Administration has ramped up its attacks on the academy, Roth has continued to publish widely, urging fellow-leaders to stand up for their principles. “Release Mahmoud Khalil! Respect freedom of speech!” he concluded in
a recent column for
Slate
, which argued that the Columbia activist’s arrest “should terrify every college president.”
Roth and I met in his office, which is dominated by a round  table where he meets with both students and his cabinet. Wearing Blundstones and polka-dot socks, he was loose-limbed and gregarious, and our conversation (which has been edited for length and clarity) was punctuated by the bright sound of batting from the baseball diamond just outside.
You wrote last year, before the election, that colleges and universities weren’t ready for what was coming. How has the reality compared to your expectations?
It’s much worse than I expected.
I had this idea—alas, it was in 2020, just as
COVID
was happening—that it would be great if colleges and universities took our civic responsibilities more seriously and really incentivized students to participate in the public sphere: work on a campaign, zoning commission, whatever. Rigorously agnostic about what they chose to work on. We found a few hundred schools that agreed in principle and we created a network. Before the 2024 election, we reactivated that group, and this time around, the institutions were much less likely to want to be publicly in support of even something so nonpartisan.
We’re really small—three thousand students or so—and I wanted University of Texas at Austin, and Michigan, other big places. Some of them did agree in principle, but this time, in 2024—in the spring, let’s say, when Biden was still in the race, it was clear Trump was going to be the candidate—th

data.title: Senior Developer Skills in the AI Age
data.author: briankelly
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了作者在个人和工作中使用AI编码工具的积极经验，这些工具帮助其团队提高了生产力和输出质量。尽管一些开发者反馈AI工具不太有效，作者认为资深开发者尤其能从中受益，因为他们的经验和知识有助于更好地利用AI。作者提出了成功使用AI编码的三个关键措施：良好结构的需求、工具based的防护机制和基于文件的关键帧管理。文中以具体项目为例，展示了AI如何独立完成编码任务，如平台问题监控项目，作者甚至在不熟悉Python的情况下，借助AI完成了整个项目。作者鼓励软件开发社区尽早接纳AI技术，以提升工作效率。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）和AI工具对软件开发的影响及开发者的态度

不同观点：
• **necovek**：对Python项目的代码质量持批评态度，认为由初级工程师编写的代码存在许多设计问题，如日志配置不当和竞态条件。总体认为该项目的代码质量较低。
• **conductr**：作为业余编程爱好者，感到LLM和“氛围编码”削弱了他对创造性编程的热情，认为LLM虽然能生成可用的代码，但剥夺了手动构建的成就感，处于一种心理困境中。
• **JohnMakin**：认为AI工具对减轻身体负担（如腱鞘炎）有帮助，但担忧未来开发技能的退化，尤其对新手开发者面临的挑战感到同情，认为未来可能只有经验丰富的“老手”才能真正理解技术细节。
• **rs186**：不赞成使用LLM生成的代码，认为调试和修正由LLM生成的错误代码耗时且不值得，宁愿自己手动编写代码以求安心。
• **only-one1701**：认为AI在绿地项目（新项目）中表现良好，但在棕地项目（已有项目的维护和扩展）中往往表现不佳，甚至比无用更糟糕。
• **sivaragavan**：强调项目前期规划的重要性，并分享使用Rust进行编译时检查的经验，认为AI生成的Rust代码中的错误有助于提前发现问题。
• **amflare**：担心过度依赖LLM会导致自身开发经验和技能的退化，认为虽然目前能有效利用LLM，但长期来看可能会失去独立编写和判断代码的能力。
• **burntcaramel**：支持LLM的使用，但强调经验丰富的开发者能更好地应对LLM生成的高“意外性”代码，提出测试驱动开发（TDD）可以帮助引导和约束AI生成的代码。
• **yoyohello13**：对AI持积极态度，认为使用Claude CLI能有效分担任务，如编写单元测试，从而提高工作效率，且不影响使用自己习惯的编辑器（neovim）。
• **jonnycoder**：认为AI工具在快速发展，建议开发者通过撰写详细的提示来获得理想的结果，并强调利用AI工具创建个人品牌的重要性，建议开发者通过创建和展示多个小型应用来提升个人影响力。
• **plandis**：在商业环境中使用LLM生成代码存在法律和知识产权问题，担心代码的版权性和公司对生成代码的法律责任，尤其是当使用第三方模型时，公司是否会承担责任。
• **vessenes**：认为当前的LLM工具能将开发者转变为架构师或CTO，但这些工具在实现良好架构方面仍存在不足，且使用过程较为繁琐和令人厌烦，导致开发过程缺乏成就感。
• **Quarrelsome**：认为文章中提到的LLM工具填补了AI在实际开发中的一些空白，尤其在水fall开发模式中表现良好，但过去缺乏合适的工具来实现这种模式。
• **scandox**：享受与人类初级开发者互动的过程，认为这种互动有助于共同成长和构建，而AI工具缺乏这种人性化的体验。
• **hinkley**：对AI工具的当前发展方向持怀疑态度，认为AI并没有解决软件开发中关于代码清晰性和可发现性的关键问题，反而可能增加负担，尤其在依赖大量第三方代码的情况下。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了LLM在绿地和棕地项目中的不同表现，以及在商业环境中使用LLM的法律和知识产权问题。
• 开发者对AI工具的态度各异，有的担忧技能退化，有的则积极利用AI提高工作效率，还有的开发者对使用AI工具缺乏成就感表示不满。
• 强调了经验丰富的开发者在有效利用LLM工具中的重要性，尤其是通过TDD和详细的提示来引导和约束AI生成的代码。

43573755.article_content:
There is a lively discussion about this post over at HackerNews:
https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=43573755
I’ve integrated some of the points made there into this article.
Introduction
Over the past few months, I have been experimenting with AI-powered coding tools in both my personal and professional projects. The experience has been overwhelmingly positive, both for me and my team of software engineers at work.
We’ve achieved better results in less time, and in many cases, the quality of our output has significantly improved.
Interestingly, this experience contrasts with the feedback I’ve received from some fellow software developers who report that AI tools aren’t working well for them.
I’m now convinced that AI-assisted software development has the potential to elevate our craft to the next level in terms of productivity. This is why I believe our community should embrace it sooner rather than later — but like all tools and practices, with the right perspective and a measured approach.
My motivation for sharing these experiences and the best practices I’ve identified is to help move the needle forward in terms of AI adoption within the broader software development community — even if realistically, it’s only by some micrometers.
The Current State of AI Coding
My Twitter feed suggests that AI-powered coding tools are already generating significant buzz in a specific niche: non-professional developers who are having great fun building software products. For them, these tools primarily serve as enablers, allowing them to tackle projects they might never have considered without such assistance.
More power to them — it’s exciting to witness their journey of struggles and breakthroughs.
However, this represents just one segment of potential users, and certainly not the only group for whom these tools can provide immense value.
The Senior Developer Advantage
My current conclusion, though preliminary in this rapidly evolving field, is that not only can seasoned developers benefit from this technology — they are actually in the optimal position to harness its power.
Here’s the important part: The very experience and accumulated know-how in software engineering and project management — which might seem obsolete in the age of AI — are precisely what enable the most effective use of these tools.
That’s because while I haven’t found the perfect metaphor for these LLM-based programming agents in an AI-assisted coding setup, I currently think of them as “an absolute senior when it comes to programming knowledge, but an absolute junior when it comes to architectural oversight
in your specific context
.”
This means that
it takes some strategic effort to make them save you a tremendous amount of work
.
And who better to invest that effort in the right way than a senior software engineer?
As we’ll see, while we’re dealing with this new, cutting-edge technology, it is the time-tested, traditional practices and tools that enable us to wield this new capability most effectively.
Three important measures for a successful AI coding session
I’ve identified three critical measures needed when working with AI-assisted coding:
Well-structured Requirements
Tool-based Guard Rails
File-based Keyframing
Before diving into these concepts, let me share some real-world examples of how I’ve used AI in my projects.
I will give examples for two categories of projects: green-field and brown-field.
For both categories, I’ll focus on cases where AI handled the entire implementation, or very nearly so.
While I do sometimes use AI as a “better autocomplete” or as a chat-only companion for general discussions, this article focuses on the “real deal” — where AI tooling operates in an agentic mode and handles all the heavy lifting.
For this, my current tool of choice is
Cursor
, powered by Anthropic’s Claude Sonnet 3.7 model. Cursor provides the crucial capability to directly edit all files in a project that require changes, and to execute commands related to the software development process.
Example 1: Platform Problem Monitoring
Cursor and Claude, combined with the expertise areas I’ll discuss below, enabled me to create and fully implement a green-field application:
Platform Problem Monitoring
. You can find the source code at
https://github.com/dx-tooling/platform-problem-monitoring-core
.
The application connects hourly to our ELK stack’s Elasticsearch server, reads the latest error messages, and sends us a well-formatted email summarizing the current state of problems on our web platform:
For more details, check out the
“New project: Platform Problem Monitoring”
post.
In this case all of the implementation logic was written by Cursor/Claude, requiring no manual code intervention from my side.
This is especially noteworthy because I don’t actually know Python. Yes, with 25+ years of software development experience, I could probably write a few lines of working Python code if pressed — but I don’t truly
know
the language. I lack the muscle
43573755.article_summary: 本文讨论了作者在个人和工作中使用AI编码工具的积极经验，这些工具帮助其团队提高了生产力和输出质量。尽管一些开发者反馈AI工具不太有效，作者认为资深开发者尤其能从中受益，因为他们的经验和知识有助于更好地利用AI。作者提出了成功使用AI编码的三个关键措施：良好结构的需求、工具based的防护机制和基于文件的关键帧管理。文中以具体项目为例，展示了AI如何独立完成编码任务，如平台问题监控项目，作者甚至在不熟悉Python的情况下，借助AI完成了整个项目。作者鼓励软件开发社区尽早接纳AI技术，以提升工作效率。
43573755.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）和AI工具对软件开发的影响及开发者的态度

不同观点：
• **necovek**：对Python项目的代码质量持批评态度，认为由初级工程师编写的代码存在许多设计问题，如日志配置不当和竞态条件。总体认为该项目的代码质量较低。
• **conductr**：作为业余编程爱好者，感到LLM和“氛围编码”削弱了他对创造性编程的热情，认为LLM虽然能生成可用的代码，但剥夺了手动构建的成就感，处于一种心理困境中。
• **JohnMakin**：认为AI工具对减轻身体负担（如腱鞘炎）有帮助，但担忧未来开发技能的退化，尤其对新手开发者面临的挑战感到同情，认为未来可能只有经验丰富的“老手”才能真正理解技术细节。
• **rs186**：不赞成使用LLM生成的代码，认为调试和修正由LLM生成的错误代码耗时且不值得，宁愿自己手动编写代码以求安心。
• **only-one1701**：认为AI在绿地项目（新项目）中表现良好，但在棕地项目（已有项目的维护和扩展）中往往表现不佳，甚至比无用更糟糕。
• **sivaragavan**：强调项目前期规划的重要性，并分享使用Rust进行编译时检查的经验，认为AI生成的Rust代码中的错误有助于提前发现问题。
• **amflare**：担心过度依赖LLM会导致自身开发经验和技能的退化，认为虽然目前能有效利用LLM，但长期来看可能会失去独立编写和判断代码的能力。
• **burntcaramel**：支持LLM的使用，但强调经验丰富的开发者能更好地应对LLM生成的高“意外性”代码，提出测试驱动开发（TDD）可以帮助引导和约束AI生成的代码。
• **yoyohello13**：对AI持积极态度，认为使用Claude CLI能有效分担任务，如编写单元测试，从而提高工作效率，且不影响使用自己习惯的编辑器（neovim）。
• **jonnycoder**：认为AI工具在快速发展，建议开发者通过撰写详细的提示来获得理想的结果，并强调利用AI工具创建个人品牌的重要性，建议开发者通过创建和展示多个小型应用来提升个人影响力。
• **plandis**：在商业环境中使用LLM生成代码存在法律和知识产权问题，担心代码的版权性和公司对生成代码的法律责任，尤其是当使用第三方模型时，公司是否会承担责任。
• **vessenes**：认为当前的LLM工具能将开发者转变为架构师或CTO，但这些工具在实现良好架构方面仍存在不足，且使用过程较为繁琐和令人厌烦，导致开发过程缺乏成就感。
• **Quarrelsome**：认为文章中提到的LLM工具填补了AI在实际开发中的一些空白，尤其在水fall开发模式中表现良好，但过去缺乏合适的工具来实现这种模式。
• **scandox**：享受与人类初级开发者互动的过程，认为这种互动有助于共同成长和构建，而AI工具缺乏这种人性化的体验。
• **hinkley**：对AI工具的当前发展方向持怀疑态度，认为AI并没有解决软件开发中关于代码清晰性和可发现性的关键问题，反而可能增加负担，尤其在依赖大量第三方代码的情况下。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了LLM在绿地和棕地项目中的不同表现，以及在商业环境中使用LLM的法律和知识产权问题。
• 开发者对AI工具的态度各异，有的担忧技能退化，有的则积极利用AI提高工作效率，还有的开发者对使用AI工具缺乏成就感表示不满。
• 强调了经验丰富的开发者在有效利用LLM工具中的重要性，尤其是通过TDD和详细的提示来引导和约束AI生成的代码。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对博尔赫斯的推荐与对其作品与人工智能（LLM）关系的探讨

不同观点：
• [viccis] 强烈推荐博尔赫斯的作品，尤其是《特隆、乌克巴尔、奥尔比斯·特蒂乌斯》这篇故事，并认为博尔赫斯的作品大多短小精悍，易于在短时间内阅读。同时，viccis 从哲学角度讨论了 LLMs 是否能创造出博尔赫斯式的知识，并引用康德的认识论，认为 LLMs 无法生成“先验综合知识”。
• [karaterobot] 提出一个假设：如果对博尔赫斯的生活进行深入了解，是否可能自然地创作出类似其风格的作品，而不是简单地模仿和复述。这引发了对 LLMs 未来创作潜力的思考。
• [101008] 认为博尔赫斯的英文翻译缺乏其原著中的诗意和音乐性，强调阅读原著的重要性。
• [6stringmerc] 提到在狱中阅读萨特的《存在与虚无》，并将萨特与博尔赫斯的哲学思想联系起来，认为 LLMs 若基于萨特的作品进行训练，可能会产生令人不安的逻辑推论，反映人类思想和行为的不足。
• [kouru225] 推荐博尔赫斯的短篇小说《福内斯的记忆》，展示了对其作品的个人喜好。
• [jhbadger] 对网站使用了一张显然是克劳德·香农的照片表示困惑，指出图片中的人并非赫伯特·西蒙。
• [tekacs] 推荐了一篇关于博尔赫斯与人工智能的论文，并提供了相关链接，引导读者进一步探讨。
• [jl6] 将博尔赫斯与人工智能、维基百科、卡夫卡、GPU、密码学等主题联系起来，展示了一种跨领域的思考方式。
• [netsharc] 认为博尔赫斯的某些故事像是对“假设”情景的报告，提出这种风格是对博尔赫斯的致敬。
• [mentalgear] 询问是否有该采访的音频文件，表示希望收听原始采访。
• [david_shi] 引用了博尔赫斯的《阿莱夫》中的一段文字，展示了博尔赫斯作品中丰富的想象力和深邃的哲学思考。
• [integralof5y] 认为博尔赫斯与赫伯特·西蒙的对话并未深入探讨人类与机器智能的关系，但承认与这样的伟人共享时间是令人愉快的。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是 LLMs 是否能生成类似博尔赫斯风格的作品，以及是否能创造出“先验综合知识”。
• 对博尔赫斯作品的翻译质量存在不同看法，有人认为英文翻译无法捕捉其原著的诗意和音乐性。
• 博尔赫斯的作品与哲学、人工智能的关系被多次提及，展示了其作品在不同领域的广泛影响和讨论潜力。
• 一些评论者提供了额外的阅读材料和资源链接，鼓励读者进一步探索博尔赫斯与人工智能的相关讨论。

data.title: Public domain technical books published before 1964
data.author: xd
data.article_summary: **Tubebooks.org** 是一个提供技术类书籍在线阅读的网站，目前收录了超过100本、总计4.22 GB的电子书，且仍在缓慢更新。网站专注于收录1964年前出版且未续版权的“真空管时代”电子书籍，其中许多书籍由网友提供。站长由于时间限制，主要依靠他人贡献扫描书籍。网站内容涵盖电气工程、音频、无线电、真空管理论与电路设计、测试与测量、被动元件等类别，书籍多为PDF格式。用户可下载书籍的部分内容预览，全书文件较大，下载需注意。若要转载，需联系站长获取许可。代表书籍包括《Applied Electronics》、《Basic Radio》、《Circuit Theory and Design》等，均为经典电子工程教材。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对旧技术书籍与现代技术书籍写作风格和质量的比较

不同观点：
• [怀旧观点] BlandDuck 认为旧的技术书籍具有独特的魅力，包括语言的直接性、细致的论证以及个人化的风格。这些书籍在技术深度和幽默感方面表现突出，而现代技术书籍往往缺乏这种特质。他提到现代教材可能在教学法上有所欠缺，导致这种差异。

• [具体实例] type0 以一本二战前的无线电电子学书籍为例，说明旧书对普通读者的友好性和写作质量。他强调，就基础概念的解释而言，现代书籍无法与旧书相媲美。

• [赞赏现代资源] dazzawazza 表达了对链接资源中无废话（no bullshit）风格的赞赏，显示出对直接、实用的技术内容的喜爱，尽管没有直接对比旧书。

补充讨论：
• 旧技术书籍的独特魅力被多位评论者提到，尤其是在语言风格和技术深度方面。
• 现代技术书籍被认为在教学法和基础概念解释上有所不足，但也有评论者对现代资源中的直接风格表示赞赏。
• 争议焦点可能在于现代技术书籍是否在质量上逊色于旧书，具体体现在写作风格和教学方法上。

43592003.article_content:
tubebooks.org
home
Technical books online!
4.22 gigabytes and still (slowly) growing!  Over 100 titles!
Preserving the Knowledge of the Ancients?
I've found that most of the technical books published before about 1964 never
had their copyrights renewed, so now are in the public domain.  So I am
endeavoring to digitize and post some selected books relating to the
"vacuum tube age" of electronics here.
Many - maybe over half now - of these books were
scanned by other people and contributed for me to post here.  Many, many
thanks to all the individuals who have helped out with this endeavor.  I
find that I do not have much time to scan books these days - the demands of the
"day job" have increased much over the past few years - so I'm not
doing a lot of scanning myself.  If you have material that you would like
to contribute, please send me an email.
I have checked to the best of my ability to confirm that these works have
expired copyrights and are now
in the public domain.  If you have information to the contrary, please
contact me at:
For information about copyrights and copyright renewals,
look
here
.  Here's a nice, easy copyright renewal
search
tool
.
For more details on how (and why)
I do this, look lower at the
bottom of
this page
.
If you want to post any of these scans on another site,
please contact me for permission before you do... I like to know who is doing
what with these things!  In general I don't have any issues with others
posting the scans that I myself have done (it might save some bandwidth),
although I do appreciate it if you credit the source of the scan.
Beware - some of these files are very big (noted with
red warnings).  If you're on dialup better start a download and go to bed!
The book scans below are
in Adobe Acrobat (PDF) format.  I recommend that if you don't already have
it you download the latest version of Adobe reader.  Some files have
compressed images that may not work correctly with older versions of Acrobat
reader.
For books containing primarily tube data, like Sylvania, GE, and
RCA tube manuals, see the
tube data page
.
Arranged by subject category,
then alphabetically by title.  Note that there is much overlap in the
subjects (e.g., many "radio" books have a thorough treatment of vacuum
tubes, and most general textbooks cover radio and vacuum tubes in some detail).  Use (ctrl-f) in your browser to find a particular book or
author...
On
most books you click on the name of the title to download an introduction (the
first few pages, usually the title through table of contents)  This way you
can see if you're interested before downloading many megabytes of data.

43592003.article_summary: **Tubebooks.org** 是一个提供技术类书籍在线阅读的网站，目前收录了超过100本、总计4.22 GB的电子书，且仍在缓慢更新。网站专注于收录1964年前出版且未续版权的“真空管时代”电子书籍，其中许多书籍由网友提供。站长由于时间限制，主要依靠他人贡献扫描书籍。网站内容涵盖电气工程、音频、无线电、真空管理论与电路设计、测试与测量、被动元件等类别，书籍多为PDF格式。用户可下载书籍的部分内容预览，全书文件较大，下载需注意。若要转载，需联系站长获取许可。代表书籍包括《Applied Electronics》、《Basic Radio》、《Circuit Theory and Design》等，均为经典电子工程教材。

data.title: Recreating Daft Punk's Something About Us
data.author: MistyMouse
data.article_summary:
本文作者在多年后重新尝试使用Ableton Live 12，并决定用它来制作一首翻唱曲，以熟悉软件。他选择了Daft Punk的《Something About Us》作为重制对象，这首歌是法国触碰（French Touch）音乐运动的代表作，该运动源于70-80年代的法国，融合了模拟与数字音效，并受到当时日本电视节目和电子音乐先锋的影响。

作者指出，法国触碰音乐的魅力在于其不完美的质感，这些质感源于当时的设备和录制环境。重现这种音效具有挑战性，因为现代工具过于精确，缺乏原版的粗糙和自发性。在重制过程中，作者选择了类似的音色和处理方式，如使用S.K.Y. Keys插件模拟Wurlitzer电钢琴，并通过简单的处理保持音色的温暖和动感。最终，作者强调，重现经典不仅在于复制音符，更在于捕捉其中的情感。

43591050.article_content:
Marca Tatem
— San Francisco, April 3rd, 2025
After years of finding it confusing and unintuitive, I finally gave
Ableton Live
another shot. With
version 12
(current as of this writing), it feels significantly more refined—so much so that it's officially become my DAW of choice.
When learning a new music production software, recreating a cover track is always a smart move. You don't have to worry too much about the songwriting itself, which frees you up to focus on the tools and the production process.
For this project, I picked a track that's emblematic of the
French Touch
movement and now nearing its 25th anniversary:
Daft Punk's
Something About Us
. Rebuilding it in a modern production environment turned out to be trickier than I expected, but here's how it went, track by track.
Wait... What's the French Touch, Anyway?
To me,
French Touch
isn't just a genre—it's a
cultural artifact
born from a very specific time and place: France in the late
'70s
and
'80s
. Its distinct sound is the product of a generation raised on
analog dreams of the digital future
.
These artists—
Daft Punk
,
Justice
,
Kavinsky
, and others—grew up immersed in a bizarre and colorful media landscape. Japanese TV shows like
X-OR
,
Sankukai
, and
Albator 84
filled French screens with space corsairs, robotic heroes, and mythological remixes set in futuristic worlds. Their themes were packed with synths, arpeggiators, and digitized voices—sounds that now echo, with a grown-up edge, in the textures of
French Touch
music.
At the same time, France was pushing into the future: science museums, open-air
electronic concerts by pioneers like
Jean-Michel Jarre
, and a sense that the 21st century was just around the corner. Yet beneath that techno-utopian veneer, cities like Paris remained gritty and raw. That tension—between the shiny and the grimy—runs deep in the DNA of
French Touch
. You hear it, especially in the darker, distorted edges of
Justice
and
Kavinsky
.
Let's also not forget the artists who laid the groundwork long before the
French Touch
became a thing. Quirky French electronic pioneers like
Jacno
, the retro-futurist charm of
Telex
from Belgium, and, of course,
Giorgio Moroder
, the godfather of
Italo Disco
—all contributed textures, tones, and sensibilities that would echo decades later. Even mainstream pop acts like
Lio
,
Étienne Daho
, or the orchestral-synth hybrids of
Rondo Veneziano
were constantly spinning on French FM radio, which in the '80s was a chaotic, genre-blurring space. This eclectic mix quietly wired an entire generation of young listeners with an appetite for melody, groove, and synthetic textures—key ingredients in what would later become
French Touch
.
Outrun never looked as good as in your dreams
There's also a certain
California dreamin
g that runs through much of
French Touch
. The imagery of Los Angeles—
endless boulevards flanked by towering palm trees and that golden sunset light
—is a romanticized vision of America that influenced the aesthetic, especially in later works. This fusion of European electronic sensibilities with American dream imagery created something uniquely transportive.
What started as a movement became a signature sound:
nostalgic, futuristic, cinematic, dirty, emotional.
Why It Was So Hard to Recreate
Part of what makes
French Touch
so compelling is also what makes it hard to replicate today. Those
lush, imperfect textures
weren't just stylistic choices—they were the natural result of a specific time, place, and set of tools. Many of these tracks were recorded in a single take, often in cramped Parisian apartments or modest studios, using vintage analog gear and early digital samplers.
There's a rawness and spontaneity to that process. The
hiss of a dusty synth
, the
unquantized groove of a looped disco break
, the warmth of
tape compression
—all of it baked into the DNA of those tracks. Today’s high-resolution digital tools are often too clean, too precise. When you remove the imperfections, you also risk scrubbing out the soul.
The Ableton Live's session
So when I set out to recreate
Something About Us
using modern software, I knew that recreating this track would be more than just copying notes or layering samples—I’d have to
chase a feeling
.
The Keys
In the original track, the keyboard part is likely played on a
Wurlitzer
electric piano
—its
signature bite and warmth
are unmistakable. For my version, I opted for something slightly different: a warmer, more rounded tone using the excellent
S.K.Y. Keys plugin
, specifically the
Everything Right
preset. It doesn't try to mimic the original exactly but brings a vibe that fits the song's emotional core.
I kept the processing minimal: just a gentle midrange boost (mainly to make the part shine a bit more on
AirPods
), a touch of Ableton's stock
Vinyl Distortion
for added warmth, and
side-chain compression
tied to the kick for subtle movement in the mix. After the intro section, I remove the bass note from the keys to carve out space for

data.title: Nebula Sans
data.author: xucheng
data.article_summary: Nebula Sans是一款现代、人文主义的无衬线字体，专为数字和印刷应用的易读性设计，基于Paul D. Hunt为Adobe Fonts设计的Source Sans。作为Nebula流媒体服务的品牌字体，Nebula Sans可作为Whitney SSm的替代品，并根据SIL开放字体许可证供免费使用。该字体提供两种样式和六种粗细，适合界面、印刷及其他多种用途。其设计初衷包括个性化、集成高级排版功能及降低商业字体许可成本。Nebula Sans在标点、风格替代及表格数字支持等方面对Source Sans进行了调整，以更好地匹配Whitney SSm。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：字体设计及其版权、字体的视觉和功能特点、免费与付费字体的对比

不同观点：
• [eps] 认为 Whitney 是一个独特且美丽的字体，但因 Hoefler 未确认共同拥有权并踢出了联合创始人 Tobias Frere-Jones，Hoefler 是“混蛋”，因此 Whitney 的免费克隆是应得的。
• [jofzar] 分享了一个关于字体数字化和版权知识的视频，并提到了一些技术细节（如 tabular-nums）。
• [lelandfe] 认为这个免费字体只是对 Whitney 做了一些调整，并提到 Source Sans 是其基础，但主要的区别在于是否需要付费。
• [davedx] 讨论了当前“中性美学”的流行趋势，虽然这种风格提供了高度可读的界面，但他怀念早期网络的混乱和活力。
• [sen] 认为该字体的营销努力与其实际创新（只是对现有字体进行了一些拉伸）不成比例。
• [anotheryou] 通过对比图指出 Whitney 看起来干净且连贯，而 Nebula Sans 则显得缺乏个性。
• [delta_p_delta_x] 详细分析了该字体与 Source Sans 的相似性，认为它不值得拥有新名字，并表达了对免费字体质量的普遍不满，强调了付费字体的价值。
• [nucleogenesis] 并不是字体爱好者，但觉得这个字体看起来很时尚，并打算将其作为默认字体。
• [dejongh] 认为字体选择是增加文本美感的重要方式，设计师应该更多地利用这个机会。
• [codedokode] 支持更多自由可用字体，但希望看到字体在小尺寸下的表现，并通过开发工具进行了测试。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于 Hoefler 和 Frere-Jones 的创始权纠纷，以及免费字体与付费字体之间的质量对比。
• 一些用户关注字体的技术特性（如 tabular-nums）和实际应用效果（如小尺寸下的可读性）。
• 对当前设计趋势（如中性美学）的看法不同，有人怀念过去的设计风格，有人接受当前的简洁风格。
• 对字体创新和营销策略的批评，认为一些新字体只是对现有设计的微调。
• 对免费字体和付费字体的详细比较，强调了高质量字体设计所需的巨大努力和成本。

43591225.article_content:
Introducing
Nebula
Sans
A versatile, modern, humanist sans-serif with a neutral aesthetic, designed for legibility in both digital and print applications.
Based on
Source Sans
by Paul D. Hunt for Adobe Fonts.
Nebula Sans is the new brand typeface for
Nebula
, the premium streaming service from independent creators. Based on
Source Sans
and designed to be a drop-in alternative to
Whitney SSm
, Nebula Sans is available for anyone to use under the SIL Open Font License.
Watch our short documentary film about the story behind Nebula Sans, written & directed by David Friedman.
Featuring two styles in six weights, Nebula Sans is well-suited for use in interfaces, print, and for any other graphical, digital, physical, metaphysical, metaphorical, or allegorical typeface needs.

Why we made this
We built our own typeface for a few key reasons:
Personalization
: we can customize the fonts to align with our preferences.
Features
: we can integrate advanced typography features tailored to our use cases.
Sustainability
: the cost of licensing commercial typefaces increases as we grow.
Source Sans was the perfect foundation for Nebula Sans because it shares many primary characteristics with
Whitney SSm
, our previous brand typeface â both were designed to bridge the gap between American gothic and European humanist typefaces, with a strong emphasis on readability. The majority of the adjustments we made were to adapt the metrics of
Source Sans
to better match those of
Whitney SSm
, since
Source Sans
is smaller and narrower by default.
Comparison of Nebula Sans versus
Whitney SSm
Typographical Details
Punctuation
The default punctuation marks in
Whitney SSm
were, to our taste, too straight. Nebula Sans uses beautiful curly glyphs from
Source Sans
.
Whitney SSm vs Nebula Sans
Stylistic Alternates
Nebula Sans features the same stylistic alternates as
Source Sans
, with the defaults aligned with those of
Whitney SSm
.

Asterisk
In typography, the asterisk symbol was named as such because it resembles a star. We love stars, so how could we not put our own spin on this little glyph?
Nebula logo
Nebula Sans asterisk
Tabular Figures
The default version of
Whitney SSm
lacks support for tabular lining figures, so we were thrilled to be able to include them in Nebula Sans. Tabular figures (or monospaced numerals) allow us to do things like increment the timestamp in the video player while keeping the digits from jumping around as they change.

• [eps] 认为 Whitney 是一个独特且美丽的字体，但因 Hoefler 未确认共同拥有权并踢出了联合创始人 Tobias Frere-Jones，Hoefler 是“混蛋”，因此 Whitney 的免费克隆是应得的。
• [jofzar] 分享了一个关于字体数字化和版权知识的视频，并提到了一些技术细节（如 tabular-nums）。
• [lelandfe] 认为这个免费字体只是对 Whitney 做了一些调整，并提到 Source Sans 是其基础，但主要的区别在于是否需要付费。
• [davedx] 讨论了当前“中性美学”的流行趋势，虽然这种风格提供了高度可读的界面，但他怀念早期网络的混乱和活力。
• [sen] 认为该字体的营销努力与其实际创新（只是对现有字体进行了一些拉伸）不成比例。
• [anotheryou] 通过对比图指出 Whitney 看起来干净且连贯，而 Nebula Sans 则显得缺乏个性。
• [delta_p_delta_x] 详细分析了该字体与 Source Sans 的相似性，认为它不值得拥有新名字，并表达了对免费字体质量的普遍不满，强调了付费字体的价值。
• [nucleogenesis] 并不是字体爱好者，但觉得这个字体看起来很时尚，并打算将其作为默认字体。
• [dejongh] 认为字体选择是增加文本美感的重要方式，设计师应该更多地利用这个机会。
• [codedokode] 支持更多自由可用字体，但希望看到字体在小尺寸下的表现，并通过开发工具进行了测试。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于 Hoefler 和 Frere-Jones 的创始权纠纷，以及免费字体与付费字体之间的质量对比。
• 一些用户关注字体的技术特性（如 tabular-nums）和实际应用效果（如小尺寸下的可读性）。
• 对当前设计趋势（如中性美学）的看法不同，有人怀念过去的设计风格，有人接受当前的简洁风格。
• 对字体创新和营销策略的批评，认为一些新字体只是对现有设计的微调。
• 对免费字体和付费字体的详细比较，强调了高质量字体设计所需的巨大努力和成本。

data.title: Cell Phone OPSEC for Border Crossings
data.author: sipofwater
data.article_summary:
这篇文章讨论了在出入境时保护手机数据的安全措施，特别是应对边境检查中对电子设备更严格的审查。作者对电脑安全有较多了解，但对手机安全知之甚少，提出了几个关键问题：如何有效删除手机上的数据（如文件、照片）以防止恢复；恢复出厂设置是否能彻底擦除数据，还是仅切断密码访问；重启后，被删文件是否仍可恢复。

对于iPhone和安卓手机，简单删除或恢复出厂设置并不总是足够安全。iPhone的加密机制较强，但仍需谨慎；安卓设备因品牌和型号不同，安全性不一。在全球范围内，反对国家权力的风险增加，保护手机数据的操作安全变得愈发重要。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何在当前环境下保护个人设备和数据安全，特别是应对执法机构或边境检查时可能遭遇的数字搜查。

不同观点：
• [技术解决方案支持者] yamrzou和dhsysusbsjsi强调具体技术手段的有效性。yamrzou分享了其Pixel 6在运行GrapheneOS时成功抵御Cellebrite等取证软件的经历，强调了强PIN码和BFU模式的保护作用。dhsysusbsjsi则建议通过关闭iPhone以及启用锁定模式来减少攻击面，以应对潜在的搜查。

• [对现实的无奈] mvdwoord对需要考虑这些安全措施的世界感到沮丧，认为这是一种不必要的心理负担，并表达了对这种生活方式的抵触情绪。

• [威胁模型的不同] decimalenough指出，现代威胁模型更多关注的是云端数据和用户凭证，而非设备本身存储的数据。传统的加密和隐藏方法已不足以应对这种新的威胁。

• [物理设备管理策略] actionfromafar提出了一种物理设备管理策略，即准备一个“伪装”手机以应对边境检查，但同时指出这种方法并非对所有人都现实或有效。

• [文化与社会评论] 1oooqooq通过引用“in soviet russia”笑话，表达了对当前状态的讽刺和无奈。

• [技术门槛与风险] vanschelven认为，对于不理解这些技术的人来说，最好不要轻易尝试，暗示了技术门槛和潜在风险。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是如何平衡个人隐私与执法需求，特别是在过境或遭遇执法检查时。
• 讨论中提到了多种技术手段和策略，但同时也反映出对普通用户而言，理解和实施这些措施具有一定难度。
• 一些评论表达了对当前数字安全环境的无奈和抵触，反映出更广泛的社会和文化问题。

43555597.article_content:
Cell Phone OPSEC for Border Crossings
I have heard stories of more aggressive interrogation of electronic devices at US border crossings. I know a lot about securing computers, but very little about securing phones.
Are there easy ways to delete data—files, photos, etc.—on phones so it can’t be recovered? Does resetting a phone to factory defaults erase data, or is it still recoverable? That is, does the reset erase the old encryption key, or just sever the password that access that key? When the phone is rebooted, are deleted files still available?
We need answers for both iPhones and Android phones. And it’s not just the US; the world is going to become a more dangerous place to oppose state power.

data.title: Pytest for Neovim
data.author: richardhapb
data.article_summary:
**pytest.nvim** 是一个为 Neovim 编辑器提供的插件，用于集成 Python 测试工具 **pytest**。它支持通过命令和快捷键在 Neovim 中运行、查看、附加或分离测试，并提供 Docker 支持，允许在容器中运行测试。

### 主要功能：
1. **运行测试**：使用 `:Pytest` 命令运行当前缓冲区的测试。
2. **查看输出**：使用 `:PytestOutput` 查看测试结果。
3. **附加测试**：使用 `:PytestAttach` 自动在保存时运行测试。
4. **Docker 支持**：通过 `:PytestEnableDocker` 和 `:PytestDisableDocker` 启用或禁用 Docker。

### 安装方法：
使用插件管理器如 **Lazyvim**、**Packer** 或 **Vim-Plug** 安装 `richardhapb/pytest.nvim`。

### 默认快捷键：
- `<leader>TT`: 运行当前文件的测试。
- `<leader>Ta`: 附加测试到当前缓冲区。
- `<leader>Td`: 从当前缓冲区分离测试。

### 配置选项：
支持自定义 Docker 容器和路径，并可通过回调函数进行高级配置。

该插件仍在开发中，未来会加入更多功能并欢迎贡献。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Neovim与pytest集成的评价及相关技术细节讨论

不同观点：
• [积极评价与项目分享]  
  - [nickandbro] 对 neovim 与 pytest 集成的赞赏，并分享了自己的业余项目 vimgolf.ai，该项目旨在教新手使用 vim 操作，目前只有两关，但计划增加更多。
  - [ohduran] 和 [meitham] 对该集成表示祝贺和赞赏。

• [技术细节与Docker相关疑问]  
  - [nickjj] 对 Docker 配置细节提出了一系列问题，包括 `print` 输出的显示位置，Docker 支持启用后的具体行为，Docker 路径和前缀的设置方式，以及 Docker Compose 支持启用与否的影响等。具体问题包括：
    1. 启用 Docker 支持是否意味着管理容器生命周期？能否仅使用 Docker 命令而不让工具管理容器？
    2. `docker_path` 是从 Docker Compose 文件中读取的卷吗？是否对应于 `WORKDIR`？
    3. `docker_path_prefix` 是否对应于 `WORKDIR` 或 `COMPOSE_PROJECT`？
    4. 如果使用 Docker Compose，容器名称是否会被忽略而使用服务名称？
    5. 支持的 Docker Compose 文件名是否应包括 `compose.yaml`？

• [其他工具的使用经验]  
  - [Jackevansevo] 分享了自己长期使用 vim 内置的 `compiler` 功能，结合 `vim-compiler-pytest` 和 `vim-dispatch`，暗示这是一种替代方案。

• [编辑器配置的调侃]  
  - [semiinfinitely] 调侃 neovim 已经“死了”，但自己仍花费大量时间配置编辑器，表达了对编辑器配置复杂性的无奈。

补充讨论：
• [改进建议]  
  - [eterps] 建议在 README 文件中说明未来改进计划，以帮助用户更好地理解项目方向。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于 Docker 支持的具体实现细节，[nickjj] 对工具的行为提出了多个疑问，特别是 Docker 容器生命周期管理和配置文件读取方式。

总结：评论主要围绕对 neovim 与 pytest 集成的赞赏与技术细节讨论，包括 Docker 配置细节的疑问和替代工具的使用经验。另外，也有对编辑器配置复杂性的调侃和改进建议。

Pytest.nvim
About the project
Testing integrated in neovim with pytest. Include Docker support. This project is in progress, I will be adding more features in the future and I open to contributions.
Getting Started
These instructions will help you set up and use
pytest.nvim
in your Neovim environment.
Prerequisites
Neovim 0.5.0 or later
pytest in your environment (pip install pytest)
Installation
Install the
pytest.nvim
plugin using your preferred plugin manager:
Lazyvim:
{
"
richardhapb/pytest.nvim
"
,
opts
=
{}
}
Packer:
use
{
"
richardhapb/pytest.nvim
"
,
opt
=
true
}
Vim-Plug:
Plug
'
richardhapb/pytest.nvim
'
Usage
Load the
pytest
plugin in your Neovim configuration if you haven't already done so. For example:
require
(
'
pytest
'
).
setup
()
Use the
:Pytest
command to run the tests in the current buffer.
To check the entire buffer:
:Pytest
To check the output of the tests:
:PytestOutput
You can attach the test to the current buffer, this runs test on save:
:PytestAttach
You can detach the test from the current buffer:
:PytestDetach
Docker enable on the way
:PytestEnableDocker
Docker disabled on the way
:PytestDisableDocker
The default keybinding that runs
:Pytest
is
<leader>T
.

- Run pytest for the current file (normal mode)
<leader>Ta
- Attach pytest to the current buffer (normal mode)
<leader>Td

43591246.article_summary:
**pytest.nvim** 是一个为 Neovim 编辑器提供的插件，用于集成 Python 测试工具 **pytest**。它支持通过命令和快捷键在 Neovim 中运行、查看、附加或分离测试，并提供 Docker 支持，允许在容器中运行测试。

### 主要功能：
1. **运行测试**：使用 `:Pytest` 命令运行当前缓冲区的测试。
2. **查看输出**：使用 `:PytestOutput` 查看测试结果。
3. **附加测试**：使用 `:PytestAttach` 自动在保存时运行测试。
4. **Docker 支持**：通过 `:PytestEnableDocker` 和 `:PytestDisableDocker` 启用或禁用 Docker。

### 安装方法：
使用插件管理器如 **Lazyvim**、**Packer** 或 **Vim-Plug** 安装 `richardhapb/pytest.nvim`。

### 默认快捷键：
- `<leader>TT`: 运行当前文件的测试。
- `<leader>Ta`: 附加测试到当前缓冲区。
- `<leader>Td`: 从当前缓冲区分离测试。

### 配置选项：
支持自定义 Docker 容器和路径，并可通过回调函数进行高级配置。

该插件仍在开发中，未来会加入更多功能并欢迎贡献。

data.title: Configuration Complexity Clock (2012)
data.author: jelder
data.article_summary: 本文通过“配置复杂度时钟”的故事，讲述了软件开发中从硬编码到复杂配置的演变过程。起初，硬编码简单直接，但随着业务变化，硬编码导致频繁的重构和部署。为解决此问题，开发者将值移到配置文件中，逐步增加复杂性，从简单的配置文件到数据库和业务规则引擎，甚至开发专用领域特定语言（DSL）。然而，过度复杂的配置和DSL最终导致技术债务和维护困难，团队发现他们回到了原点，只是现在用的是一种更差的“语言”。作者提醒，在复杂度达到一定程度时，硬编码可能是相对较好的选择，不应盲目追求复杂的配置方案，而应考虑改进构建-测试-部署流程。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于配置语言（DSL）与直接编码的优劣以及配置管理的复杂性

不同观点：
• **支持使用DSL**：
   - MoreQARespect认为应遵守"最小权限规则"，通过构建DSL来处理简单配置，但如果需求变得复杂（如需要循环或条件判断），应转回编写常规代码。
   - Xmd5a支持使用DSL，并提出了一种函数式DSL设计模式，允许自由组合配置行为，同时避免复杂实现。

• **反对DSL，支持直接使用编程语言**：
   - jstanley反对将配置移到配置文件，认为除非必要，否则应将配置和代码放在一起，以提高可读性和调试效率。
   - oftenwrong批评了过度追求可配置性而导致配置实际上变成代码的荒谬现象，认为现代软件可以通过随时部署来避免这种复杂性。

• **对DSL和直接编码之间保持平衡**：
   - CraigJPerry正在探索组合性，避免使用DSL，但仍在寻找让用户用自己熟悉语言进行配置的方法。
   - praptak相信存在一种理想化的配置语言，既不是编程语言但又足够表达，如Jsonnet，但强调需要良好的判断来决定哪些内容应放入配置。

• **环境变量与配置文件的争议**：
   - rednafi认为环境变量调试困难，建议使用简单的文本文件进行配置，以减少认知负担。
   - feelamee和zevv认为使用小型现有语言（如Lua）作为DSL可以兼顾简单性和灵活性，且不同于硬编码。

补充讨论：
• **关于DSL的目标用户和使用场景**：
   - bob1029分享了项目中使用不同DSL的经验，强调需要考虑目标用户（如业务人员）的理解能力和需求，最终倾向于使用SQL以获得更好接受度。
   - myst提到Emacs作为一个从一开始就使用DSL的例子，展示了DSL在实际应用中的长期演化。

争议焦点：
• **DSL的复杂性与可维护性**：
   - 一方认为DSL会增加系统复杂性和认知负担（如jstanley和oftenwrong）。
   - 另一方认为好的DSL设计可以提供更具表达力的解决方案，并减少重复编码（如MoreQARespect和Xmd5a）。

• **配置与代码的边界**：
   - 讨论了配置应靠近代码还是独立管理的问题，关注点在于可维护性和调试效率（如jstanley和rednafi）。

整体讨论围绕DSL的优缺点、配置管理策略的选择及其在不同场景中的适用性展开。

43555760.article_content:
When I was a young coder, just starting out in the big scary world of enterprise software, an older, far more experienced chap gave me a stern warning about hard coding values in my software. “They
will
have to change at some point, and you don’t want to recompile and redeploy your application just to change the VAT tax rate.” I took this advice to heart and soon every value that my application needed was loaded from a huge .ini file. I still think it’s good advice, but be warned, like most things in software, it’s good advice
up to a point
. Beyond that point lies pain.
Let me introduce you to my ‘Configuration Complexity Clock’.
This clock tells a story. We start at midnight, 12 o’clock, with a simple new requirement which we quickly code up as a little application. It’s not expected to last very long, just a stop-gap in some larger strategic scheme, so we’ve hard-coded all the application’s values. Months pass, the application becomes widely used, but there’s a problem, some of the business values change, so we find ourselves rebuilding and re-deploying it just to change a few numbers. This is obviously wrong. The solution is simple, we’ll move those values out into a configuration file, maybe some appsettings in our App.config. Now we’re at 2 on the clock.
Time passes and our application is now somewhat entrenched in our organisation. The business continues to evolve and as it does, more values are moved to our configuration file. Now appsettings are no longer sufficient, we have groups of values and hierarchies of values. If we’re good, by now we will have moved our configuration into a dedicated XML schema that gets de-serialized into a configuration model. If we’re not so good we might have shoe-horned repeated and multi-dimensional values into some strange tilda and pipe separated strings. Now we’re at 4 or 5 on the clock.
More time passes, the irritating ‘chief software architect’ has been sacked and our little application is now core to our organisation. The business rules become more complex and so does our configuration. In fact there’s now a considerable learning curve before a new hire can successfully carry out a deployment. One of our new hires is a very clever chap, he’s seen this situation before. “What we need is a business rules engine” he declares. Now this looks promising. The configuration moves from its XML file into a database and has its own specialised GUI. Initially there was hope that non-technical business users would be able to use the GUI to configure the application, but that turned out to be a false hope; the mapping of business rules into the engine requires a level of expertise that only some members of the development team possess. We’re now at 6 on the clock.
Frustratingly there are still some business requirements that can’t be configured using the new rules engine. Some logical conditions simply aren’t configurable using its GUI, and so the application has to be re-coded and re-deployed for some scenarios. Help is at hand, someone on the team reads
Ayende’s DSLs book
. Yes, a DSL will allow us to write arbitrarily complex rules and solve all our problems. The team stops work for several months to implement the DSL. It’s a considerable technical accomplishment when it’s completed and everyone takes a well earned break. Surely this will mean the end of arbitrary hard-coded business logic? It’s now 9am on the clock.
Amazingly it works. Several months go by without any changes being needed in the core application. The team spend most of their time writing code in the new DSL. After some embarrassing episodes, they now go through a complete release cycle before deploying any new DSL code. The DSL text files are version controlled and each release goes through regression testing before being deployed. Debugging the DSL code is difficult, there’s little tooling support, they simply don’t have the resources to build an IDE or a ReSharper for their new little language. As the DSL code gets more complex they also start to miss being able to write object-oriented software. Some of the team have started to work on a unit testing framework in their spare time.
In the pub after work someone quips, “we’re back where we started four years ago, hard coding everything, except now in a much crappier language.”
They’ve gone around the clock and are back at 12.
Why tell this story? To be honest, I’ve never seen an organisation go all the way around the clock, but I’ve seen plenty that have got to 5, 6, or 7 and feel considerable pain. My point is this:
At a certain level of complexity, hard-coding a solution may be the least evil option.
You already have a general purpose programming language, before you go down the route of building a business rules engine or a DSL, or even if your configuration passes a certain level of complexity, consider that with a slicker build-test-deploy cycle, it might be far simpler just to hard code it.

主要讨论点：用户对一个益智游戏的界面、规则理解、功能建议及多解决方案的争议

不同观点：
• **游戏界面和规则不清晰**：
  - [rstarast] 认为界面让逻辑解谜变得困难，分享了外部链接以帮助理解。
  - [riffraff] 表示在移动端上不明白游戏目标，建议添加教程或提示按钮。
  - [albert_e] 也提到作为非英语母语者，很难理解数字的含义。

• **自主探索规则的优劣**：
  - [laurentlb] 同意规则不清晰，但认为自主探索是游戏的一部分，建议添加引导但不要直接给出答案。

• **具体规则的理解**：
  - [monkeycantype] 澄清了误解，指出游戏的核心目标是根据数字提示隐藏或显示方块，并解释了红色数字的含义。

• **功能改进建议**：
  - [andrelaszlo] 建议添加标记或锁定已确定单元格的功能。
  - [lindenr] 提出允许标记内部单元格，以减少用户记忆负担，并赞赏了游戏在大尺寸下的拓扑复杂性。

• **多解决方案的争议**：
  - [mcphage] 指出游戏存在多个可能的解决方案，给出了一个具体例子，表明某些部分既可以包含在循环内也可以排除在外。

补充讨论：
• **总体评价**：
  - [HeavyStorm] 和 [readthenotes1] 对游戏表示了积极的评价，认为其有趣且有成瘾性。
  
• **对算法的好奇**：
  - [IJ92] 对 puzzle 生成算法表示好奇，并希望了解更多技术细节。

data.title: Clawtype: Custom wearable chorded keyboard and mouse
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: "Clawtype" 是一个开源的可穿戴弦键盘和鼠标项目，基于 SparkFun ProMicro RP2040 板开发，使用 Rust 嵌入式编程。它是 Chordite 键盘的一个变种，包含自定义的 3D 打印部件设计。项目遵循 AGPL-3.0 许可证，贡献代码需遵循相同许可协议。主要技术包括 Rust、C 和 C++，目前有 15 个星标和 1 个分支。更多信息和视频演示可访问相关链接。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于无表键盘（tableless gloves）的设计及其按键布局的讨论

43590775.article_summary: "Clawtype" 是一个开源的可穿戴弦键盘和鼠标项目，基于 SparkFun ProMicro RP2040 板开发，使用 Rust 嵌入式编程。它是 Chordite 键盘的一个变种，包含自定义的 3D 打印部件设计。项目遵循 AGPL-3.0 许可证，贡献代码需遵循相同许可协议。主要技术包括 Rust、C 和 C++，目前有 15 个星标和 1 个分支。更多信息和视频演示可访问相关链接。

data.title: Quaker Parents Were Ahead of Their Time
data.author: ggm
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了作者在1991年的一次童年经历：为了喝到冰镇的Diet Mountain Dew，他把一罐可乐放进微波炉，结果引发了火灾。事后，作者的母亲并没有责骂他，而是表扬了他的诚实和责任感。这一事件反映了作者家庭作为贵格会信徒的价值观——避免评判，采用积极强化。多年后，作者成为一名记者，专注于育儿和教育，发现这些价值观与儿童发展研究相吻合。贵格会强调简朴、和平、诚信、社区、平等和 stewardship 等原则，并通过提问引导孩子自主决策，培养他们的自律和解决问题的能力。这种育儿方式有助于孩子 emotional health、学业表现和社会交往能力。尽管完全的自主权有风险，但贵格会也强调智慧和爱心的管教。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：是否应该传播贵格会（Quaker）的价值观，以及如何平衡不主动传教和希望世界变得更好的愿望。

不同观点：
• **支持有限度传播价值观**：teaearlgraycold 认为，虽然贵格会传统上不鼓励积极传教，但他个人认为世界会因为更多贵格会信徒而变得更好。他选择通过分享个人价值观的方式，希望对世界产生积极影响。这种观点强调个人行动的影响力，但不主张强制性传教。

• **传统不传教立场**：贵格会传统上不支持积极传教，这表明一些贵格会信徒可能认为信仰应该是个人选择，不应通过外在力量去影响他人。这种立场尊重每个人的信仰选择自由，强调内在的精神修行而非外在的扩张。

补充讨论：
• **个人价值观的传播方式**：teaearlgraycold 提到通过分享个人价值观来影响他人，而不是通过传统的传教方式。这表明了一种温和的、非侵入性的传播信仰或价值观的方式。

• **争议焦点**：争议的核心在于如何在尊重贵格会不传教传统的同时，表达希望世界因更多贵格会信徒而变得更好的愿望。这涉及到个人信仰表达与宗教传统之间的平衡问题。

One morning in 1991, I prayed with the fervor that only a tween can muster for one thing above all others: cold Diet Mountain Dew. But all of the cans in my mom’s stash were warm. So I tossed one in the freezer, forgot about it, and hours later retrieved the frozen-solid mass. Then I decided to pop it in the microwave. You can imagine what ensued.
After extinguishing the flames, my mom asked us kids what we thought had happened. I stepped forward as if approaching the gallows—and she lavished me with praise. For telling the truth. For taking responsibility. Her response might seem surprising, but we’re Quakers, and avoiding judgment is pretty on-brand.
From where I stand now, I can see that her decision to use positive reinforcement aligns with research on motivating kids, something I’ve become quite familiar with as a journalist covering parenting and education. Still, for years, I didn’t recognize the connection between my faith and the child-development studies I frequently combed through at work. Then, when the coronavirus pandemic temporarily left our public school
without enough adults
to meet my son’s needs, we switched him to a Quaker school. The school is organized around an acronym I’d never heard before—
SPICES
—that stands for principles I know well: simplicity, peace, integrity, community, equality, and stewardship. Those
aren’t the only
pillars of Quakerism, but they’re big ones, and seeing them all together got me thinking. Sitting in the meetinghouse one Sunday morning, after nearly an hour of silent worship, I had a
Queen’s Gambit
moment. Whereas the chess champ saw pawns moving across a phantom board, I saw each child-rearing best practice I’d been writing about line up with a principle of Quakerism.
The Religious Society of Friends—“Quaker” being a derogatory term, reclaimed—is a hard faith to explain, because it tries to eschew dogma. It’s now possible to be a Muslim Quaker or a Hindu one, or to not believe in any god at all. That said, Quakers all over the world tend to talk about the same principles and take part in some of the same practices. For example, in place of rules, Quakers publish “advices and queries,” which prompt individuals to make good, considered choices. Attendees of Quaker meetings near me were recently asked to ponder: “Do I make my home a place of friendliness, joy, and peace, where residents and visitors feel God’s presence?” The children’s version read: “In what ways am I kind to people in my home?” Certain expectations underlie these questions—that one should try to be kind, for example—but so do curiosity and an openness to differing answers.
As it turns out, leading with questions is a great way for parents to talk to children. Encouraging kids to come up with their own solutions grants them autonomy. And as Emily Edlynn, a psychologist and the author of
Autonomy-Supportive Parenting
, told me, kids who feel like they have
control over their life
experience
better
emotional health
, including
less
depression and anxiety. Fostering kids’ autonomy has also been tied to children building stronger
self-regulation
skills, doing better
in school, and navigating
social situations more effectively. Best of all, once kids get used to the self-discipline that comes with exercising autonomy, it can become habitual. Give your kids agency in one area, and they tend to “develop internal motivation even for things that they do not want to do,” Edlynn said, “because they’re integrating the understanding of the ‘why’ those things are so important.”
Read: The teen-disengagement crisis
It can be scary to trust children with independence. But kids are better problem-solvers than some people might think. When my son, at age 10, asked me if he could play laser tag with friends, I asked him how he could avoid pulling a trigger (in deference to the Quaker value of pacifism). He decided to serve as referee. I was proud of him for exercising “
discernment
,” another Quaker value, all on his own, for listening to his “still, small voice within” and letting it guide him to a solution that satisfied his need for belonging. He is now 13 and recently couldn’t decide whether to accept a babysitting job or relax at home. I asked him, “What do you think tomorrow-you will wish today-you had done?” He picked out stuffed animals to give his charges, spent the evening feeling needed, and had cash the next day when he wanted to buy boba for a friend.
Obviously, real damage could come from giving kids
complete
autonomy, and Quakerism recognizes this. Early Quaker epistles inveigh against permissiveness, and a 1939 text,
Children & Quakerism
, quotes William Penn, the Quaker who founded Pennsylvania, saying, “If God give you children, love them with wisdom, correct them with affection.” In other words, pacifism doesn’t mean that parents can’t set boundaries. As a 1967

data.title: Supervisors often prefer rule breakers, up to a point
data.author: rustoo
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：规则的制定与打破及其在不同情境下的合理性

不同观点：
• pdpi认为规则通常伴随着妥协，为了让人类能够理解，规则必须相对简单。简单的规则在复杂情况下会禁止一些好的行为，并允许一些坏的行为。社会中的“寄生虫”往往利用“允许的坏行为”空间，但探索“被禁止的好行为”也有其价值。

• ike2792指出，在大型组织中，规则分为两类：1) 拖慢 everyone 进度的繁文缛节，2) 绝对不能打破的重要规则。高效的人学会区分这两类规则，以打破不必要的繁文缛节来提高工作效率。

• seeknotfind提出，理解规则制定的原因并确保规则制定者会对此满意是关键，这一观点仅适合高层人员。

• madrox作为主管，表示更愿意信任员工的判断和内在动机，而不是强制执行规则。只有在员工的判断力不再被信任时，才会使用规则来外在地激励他们。

• RunSet引用了“超级 incompetence”和“超级 competence”的例子，说明两者都会破坏等级制度，甚至会导致解雇。

• anthmotb分享了一个早期职业生涯的故事，说明在资源不足的情况下，适度打破规则可以推进工作，但需要承担一定后果。

• taeric认为，有目的地打破规则不一定是坏事，但失败之处在于当“成本”判断无法与上级达成一致时。

• rblatz通过职业运动员使用类固醇的例子，说明有些规则的打破实际上是被默许的，因为它们有助于控制某些局面。

• neilv指出，规则的起源和组织对其的重视程度会影响规则的可打破性，并强调不同情境下规则的灵活性。

• neuroelectron认为，规则的打破者可以带来收益而无需承担责任。

• jillesvangurp对比了德国和荷兰对规则的不同态度，认为适时打破过时规则是一种适应变化的智慧。

• smeej表示，无法在超过三层管理架构下工作，因为过多的规则会妨碍工作效率，更适合在初创企业工作。

• terramars质疑关于规则打破与团队胜利关系的研究结论，并举例说明在某些情况下规则的打破并不一定导致失败。

• gwern引用了“合同的不完整性”概念，说明规则无法涵盖所有可能的情况，适度的规则打破有时对组织是有益的。

• ungreased0675认为，该研究仅适用于NHL，难以推广到其他情境。

补充讨论：
规则的合理性和可打破性在不同组织和文化中存在差异，不同情境下对规则的不同态度可能导致不同的结果。规则的执行与打破需要权衡具体情况和潜在后果。

• Fathom公司强调其AI笔记应用的快速增长和团队的高效协作文化，特别提到适合那些喜欢与经验丰富的同事合作并快速交付产品的人。（观点2：强调团队文化与快速产品交付）
• Sheer Health公司专注于解决医疗账单和保险沟通问题，提供多个后端、全栈和机器学习相关的职位，强调对技术栈的灵活要求并提供较高的薪酬。（观点3：关注医疗领域技术解决方案与高薪酬）
• Langfuse公司作为开放源代码的LLMOps工具提供商，强调其对复杂工程挑战的优雅解决方案，并寻求在柏林本地工作的工程师。（观点4：专注于LLMOps工具开发与本地招聘）
• SolutionStreet公司提供多种远程和混合角色，强调对Python、DevOps和.NET等技术的需求，并注重项目管理和团队协作能力。（观点5：注重技术深度与项目管理能力）
• Stealth AI Healthcare Startup公司作为一家初创公司，强调其快速发展的技术栈和AI应用，寻求能独立解决问题的全栈工程师，提供高拥有权的工作环境。（观点6：初创公司环境与全栈工程师需求）
• AbbVie公司提供AI/软件工程师职位，强调团队合作与AI/LLM技术的应用，并注重候选人在数据工程方面的能力。（观点7：关注AI与数据工程结合的职位需求）

data.title: Commercial Kitchen Industry Overview and Models
data.author: mooreds
data.article_summary: 共享厨房已成为推动食品创新、经济发展和社区成长的重要枢纽。它们不仅提供烹饪空间，还通过灵活、经济的解决方案支持餐饮创业者实现创业梦想。共享厨房帮助初创企业降低风险，通过市场测试概念，避免高昂的自建成本，并随着业务增长调整策略。不同类型的共享厨房，如共享商用厨房、孵化器厨房、幽灵厨房等，满足了多样化的食品销售需求，促进地方就业、劳动力发展和食品安全。它们为缺乏资源的个人和小企业提供关键基础设施，并随着食品交付服务兴起和疫情影响而不断调整运营模式。共享厨房不仅推动创业创新，还通过支持本地农场、增加健康食品的获取和促进社区繁荣，成为改变社区的重要力量。调查显示，55%的共享厨房成员为女性，47%为少数族裔，显示其在创造包容性经济机会方面的潜力。

Industry Overview and Models
In recent years, shared kitchens have emerged as dynamic hubs for food innovation, economic development, and community growth. In their many forms, these kitchens are more than just spaces to prepare meals—they are the backbone of thriving local food ecosystems. From budding chefs and small-scale producers to established culinary businesses, shared kitchens offer accessible, flexible, and cost-effective solutions for food entrepreneurs
to turn their visions into reality.
By providing a space to test ideas and refine products, shared kitchens help startups de-risk their business. They allow them to market-test their concepts without the high upfront costs of building their own facilities. This model enables food entrepreneurs to launch and grow, adjusting as they learn and mitigating financial risk along the way.
Shared commercial kitchens, incubator kitchens, food truck commissaries, ghost kitchens, and food processing centers cater to the growing demand for culinary diversity across sales channels. Each plays a unique role in local economies by fostering job creation, workforce development, and greater food security for local communities. These spaces provide essential infrastructure for individuals and small businesses that might not have the resources to navigate the complexities of opening a food production space of their own.
Shared kitchen facilities have rapidly evolved. Once a novel concept, they are now diverse and integrated into various community spaces. From standalone facilities to components within markets, community centers, or housing projects, today’s shared kitchens offer many amenities, including event spaces, culinary studios, and cafes. They serve many businesses, including food trucks, bakers, caterers, ghost kitchen concepts, meal kits, and consumer packaged goods (CPG).
Shared kitchen facilities have rapidly evolved. Once a novel concept, they are now diverse and integrated into various community spaces.
This chapter explores the varied landscape of shared kitchen models and their impact on communities—whether by driving entrepreneurial innovation, supporting local farms, or providing access to healthy, locally produced foods. As flexible spaces, shared kitchens have adapted to industry shifts, such as the rise of food delivery services and the rapid adjustments required during the COVID-19 pandemic. This has reshaped how they operate today, spurring refinement and innovation in kitchen models. Whether you’re a community seeking to foster economic growth through local food initiatives or an entrepreneur looking for the right kitchen model to launch or scale your business, this chapter offers valuable insights. We provide a framework to understand the unique opportunities and challenges of each model, helping you identify the best fit for your local needs. More than just facilities, these kitchens are key drivers of change—building prosperity, resilience, and community well-being, one meal at a time.
Shared Kitchen Industry
Shared kitchens are licensed commercial spaces that provide a pathway for food entrepreneurs—from chefs, caterers, food truck operators, and bakers to value-added producers and packaged food and beverage makers—to launch and grow their businesses. Shared kitchens and incubator kitchens play a unique and vital role in food systems and entrepreneurial ecosystems across the country. By providing entrepreneurs, producers, and food access programs with affordable space, shared kitchens help strengthen local food systems and build community prosperity. They are valuable tools for achieving a wide range of community goals, including job creation, workforce training, increased access to healthy food and nutrition education, support for local farms, a more localized food economy, neighborhood revitalization, and even tourism.
Shared kitchens are also powerful launchpads for entrepreneurship. By renting space in a shared kitchen on an hourly, daily, or monthly basis, businesses can produce food in compliance with regulatory requirements without needing to invest in their own facility during a stage when capital and cash flow are a challenge. Similarly, incubator kitchens provide access to production space while also delivering education and ecosystem services that support business success, lower barriers, and propel growth. As these businesses grow, they create jobs for the local community and often support local farmers and producers through their purchasing. Many successful shared kitchen members go on to establish their own brick-and-mortar businesses, contributing to the vibrancy of neighborhoods and local economies. These new businesses create jobs, stimulate tourism, and further enrich the food scene.

data.title: How Big Is VMS?
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了VMS操作系统的大小，特别是其源代码的行数。作者通过编写程序统计了不同版本（V6.2、V7.2、V8.2、V9.2-3）中15个核心组件的源代码行数，排除了空白行和注释行。结果显示，这些组件在V8.2版本中总计约166,678行代码，且在多个版本中代码量增加了近三倍，每个版本平均增加约400,000行代码。VMS最初使用BLISS和MACRO-32编写，后逐步转向C语言。作者指出，VMS包含409个设施，代码量增长显著，特别是在Alpha和x86架构的移植过程中。文章最后邀请读者提出未来研究建议。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：VMS（虚拟内存系统）的当前实用性、历史发展及其相关技术细节

不同观点：
• **VMS的实用性存疑**：jamesy0ung认为，除了无法迁移的遗留应用外，VMS在今天没有太多实际用途。他提到VMS的1年期虚拟机许可很烦人，并认为相比主流的Linux，VMS显得过时且小众，用户会被VSI（VMS软件公司）锁定。

• **对VMS历史及技术贡献的尊重**：markus_zhang对VMS的设计者David Cutler表示敬佩，强调他在操作系统设计方面的专业性，并询问Cutler是否仍在微软工作，表现出对技术专家的个人崇拜和对其工作的兴趣。

• **VMS的历史失败与怀旧情感**：snovymgodym详细回顾了VMS的历史，认为它错过了多个技术发展机遇，包括Unix的崛起、Alpha和Itanium处理器的失败。尽管如此，他仍对VMS可能的开源释放抱有希望。

• **对VMS的情感与怀旧**：uptownfunk对VMS（VAX）表示感激，因为它曾为其家庭提供了经济支持。这种情感性怀旧让他对VMS持有正面态度， regardless of its obsolescence.

• **技术细节与代码量质疑**：whartung对ACPI代码量在VMS代码库中的占比表示质疑，提到ACPI部分的代码行数高达165K，认为这可能过多。

• **VMS版本的澄清**：zabzonk要求明确讨论的是VAX VMS，暗示可能存在不同版本的混淆。

• **对VMS知识产权和用户体验的不满**：ConanRus批评VMS持有者对遗留知识产权的管理不善，特别是对爱好者的支持不足。他还提到目前只能通过每6个月重新下载和设置VM镜像来维持使用，并批评VMS方面抱怨开源贡献不足。

补充讨论：
• VMS的历史发展中多次错失技术趋势，导致其目前被视为遗留系统。
• 不同用户对VMS的情感态度存在分歧，一些人认为它已经过时，另一些人则对其怀有感激和尊重。
• 技术细节如ACPI代码量引发了一些对VMS技术实现的质疑。
• 对VMS知识产权管理和用户支持的批评反映了用户体验和社区参与的问题。

争议焦点：VMS在现代计算环境中的实用性及其管理和支持问题。

43573738.article_content:
How Big Is VMS?
This question was asked during my Boot Camp presentation last fall in Boston, and over the past 35 years dozens of times people have asked, how big is VMS? That translates into "how many lines of code are in VMS"? I thought it was time to at least make a stab at pursuing some insight into the answer. I wrote some command procedures to count the number of source lines in .B32, .B64, .C, .MAR, .M64, and .S files. Not counted are blank lines and lines beginning with the standard comment characters and miscellaneous directives for the particular language.
First, I needed a baseline definition of  'VMS'.
Does it include layered products, networking, compilers, RTLs, debuggers, open source, etc.?
Is it the code on a particular running system?
Does it include command procedures?
I said 'no' to all of the above and as a starting point chose 15 facilities which are representative of identifiable components of the system: ACPI , AUDSRV, CLUSTER, DCL, DRIVER, F11X, JOBCTL, LAN, PCSI, RMS, SCSI, SDA, SHADOWING, SYS, XFC.
I chose the following releases for comparison:
V6.2:       May / 1995 - port to Alpha
V7.2:       Feb / 1999 - kernel threads, 64-bit APIs, Galaxy, and more
V8.2:       Feb /  2005 - port to Itanium
V9.2-3:     Dec / 2024 - port to x86
The LINES.COM procedure, which invokes a set of nested procedures, fetches all of the source files with the extensions mentioned above, in the SCSI facility that are in the release stream V8.2, gets the line counts, and produces the text file below. This was done for each of the 15 facilities in each of the four release streams.
MTMERU-V8.4-2L2$ @lines scsi "V8.2" V82
MTMERU-V8.4-2L2$ type [.scsi]total-line-counts-v82.txt
WORK10:[GRANT.LOC.SCSI.BLISS]TOTALS.TXT;1
Total source files = 2
Total source lines = 7770
WORK10:[GRANT.LOC.SCSI.C]TOTALS.TXT;1
Total source files = 64
Total source lines = 119609
WORK10:[GRANT.LOC.SCSI.M64]TOTALS.TXT;1
Total source files = 1
Total source lines = 885
WORK10:[GRANT.LOC.SCSI.MAR]TOTALS.TXT;1
Total source files = 34
Total source lines = 38414
WORK10:[GRANT.LOC.SCSI.S]TOTALS.TXT;1
Total source files = 0
Total source lines = 0
Grand Totals
Total source files = 101
Total source lines = 166678
MTMERU-V8.4-2L2$
Here are all the totals for V8.2. There is a similar chart for each of the other three releases.
Here is the lines of code summary for the four releases. You can find a graphical representation of the table below at this
link
.
Notes and Observations:
Not all code in a facility is in every release, but it is or has been in one or more releases.
There are 409 facilities in the VMS source pool - some big, some small. They contribute to the VMS operating system build for one or more platforms.
These 15 facilities chosen comprise close to two million lines of code and their total has nearly tripled in size during the last three releases.
There were many changes and additions to VMS between V8.2 and V9.2-3 prior to the x86 porting work.
Given a relatively small delta, each release has increased by about 400,000 lines of code.
The emergence of C code is another aspect of VMS that is part of the story. In the beginning, VMS was written in BLISS and MACRO-32 (VAX assembler). During the latter stages of the port to Alpha, we declared that all new code would be written in C. There are exceptions, of course, but for the most part we followed this guideline. Not shown in the data above, but part of this investigation, is the following which reflects the 15 facilities. (The 31 C modules in V6.2 were all written during the port to Alpha.)
It might be interesting to look into why some facilities have changed so much over time. Some seem obvious but others do not. If you have suggestions for a future post, please speak up.
Mar 31st, 2025
Clair Grant
VMS Researcher

• **对VMS知识产权和用户体验的不满**：ConanRus批评VMS持有者对遗留知识产权的管理不善，特别是对爱好者的支持不足。他还提到目前只能通过每6个月重新下载和设置VM镜像来维持使用，并批评VMS方面抱怨开源贡献不足。

补充讨论：
• VMS的历史发展中多次错失技术趋势，导致其目前被视为遗留系统。
• 不同用户对VMS的情感态度存在分歧，一些人认为它已经过时，另一些人则对其怀有感激和尊重。
• 技术细节如ACPI代码量引发了一些对VMS技术实现的质疑。
• 对VMS知识产权管理和用户支持的批评反映了用户体验和社区参与的问题。

争议焦点：VMS在现代计算环境中的实用性及其管理和支持问题。

data.title: I maintain a 17 year old ThinkPad
data.author: Fred34
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了为什么作者仍然使用一台17年前的Thinkpad笔记本电脑，并将其与现代MacBook进行对比。文章引用了Nassim Nicholas Taleb的“反脆弱”理论和Lindy效应，指出像旧Thinkpad这样 longevity设计的产品具有“抗脆弱性”，因为其模块化设计允许用户轻松更换部件，如电池、内存和存储驱动器，从而延长使用寿命。Thinkpad的坚固做工和开放生态系统使其能够承受日常磨损而不过时。相比之下，现代MacBook虽然性能强大，但其设计更为“脆弱”，许多组件是焊接的，难以维修或更换，且依赖于苹果的软件支持。一旦硬件或软件支持终止，MacBook更容易变得不可用。因此，作者认为旧Thinkpad因其耐用性和可修复性更具优势。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：ThinkPad与Framework笔记本的比较，以及旧硬件的可持续使用与升级潜力

不同观点：
• CursedSilicon认为，ThinkPad在二手市场的成功源于其耐用性和可升级性，但随着时间推移，旧型号硬件逐渐难以满足现代需求。Framework笔记本虽然具有类似的优势，但作为小众品牌，其入门成本较高。
• zokier指出，超过10年以上的旧笔记本如T440之前的型号在功能和性能上存在显著缺陷，而T450系列在许多关键规格上仍有较好的表现，可以作为长期使用的选择。
• quailfarmer主张，硬件的高度集成是提升性能、成本和可靠性的关键，模块化设计并非必要。他以Apple为例，认为Framework应在不牺牲集成优势的前提下追求可修复性。
• dpedu分享了MacBook电池更换的个人经验，指出不同型号的难度有所不同，较新的型号相对容易。
• mtlmtlmtlmtl强调了ThinkPad在防尘设计上的优势，认为其良好的散热设计和保护显示屏的能力是其长寿的重要因素。
• interroboink提到，旧硬件面临的最大问题是操作系统和软件支持的终结，这会限制设备的可使用范围。
• ajxs表达了对ThinkPad x220的深厚感情，认为其耐用性和键盘手感使其在多年后仍然优于一些现代笔记本。
• ruleryak展示了其1997年ThinkPad 760 XL的持续可用性，强调了老旧硬件的持久性。
• anon6362详细描述了其T480的升级和改装，展示了通过硬件更换和外部设备提升老旧笔记本性能的可能性。
• tyushk希望Lenovo能推出类似T420但配备现代显示屏和内部硬件的笔记本，并对现有的核心硬件升级项目表示关注。
• ivraatiems分享了其翻新和出售旧ThinkPad的经验，认为即使是现代型号也具有良好的耐用性和市场价值。
• markus_zhang表示其T470S在Ubuntu环境下表现良好，但图形驱动存在问题，且对风扇未进行维护。
• johnisgood询问如何清除遗忘的ThinkPad T42超级管理员密码，希望继续使用这台状态良好的旧笔记本。
• randerson怀念其被公司政策强制报废的ThinkPad X220，认为这是一种不必要的浪费。
• frfl抱怨难以找到耐用的ThinkPad替代电池，对购买的电池寿命不满。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及的争议焦点包括旧硬件的性能和功能是否足以满足现代需求，以及模块化设计与高度集成设计之间的优劣比较。
• 用户对ThinkPad的耐用性和升级潜力给予高度评价，但对其电池寿命和某些硬件缺陷也提出了一些抱怨。
• Framework笔记本被视为一种具有潜力的现代替代方案，但其市场地位和入门成本成为讨论中的关注点。

43564111.article_content:
Why I Maintain a 17 Year Old Thinkpad
Published on: April 1, 2025
If a book has been in print for forty years, I can expect it to be in print for another forty years. But, and that is the main difference, if it survives another decade, then it will be expected to be in print another fifty years. This, simply, as a rule, tells you why things that have been around for a long time are not "aging" like persons, but "aging" in reverse. Every year that passes without extinction doubles the additional life expectancy. This is an indicator of some robustness. The robustness of an item is proportional to its life
― Nassim Nicholas Taleb, Antifragile
Nassim Nicholas Taleb contrasts
fragile
systems—those that suffer serious harm under volatility—with
robust
systems that can endure stress with minimal damage. He extends this concept with
antifragile
systems, which can actually benefit from disorder, but we’ll focus here on the divide between fragile and robust.
Taleb also introduces the
Lindy Effect
as an idea about longevity: if something non-perishable has been around for a long time, that track record suggests it’s likely to keep going. We’ll see how this relates to two laptops—one from 2008, the other from 2021.
Old Thinkpads: Modular, Robust Survivors
IBM and early Lenovo Thinkpads showcases a design built for longevity. Despite their age, these business-class laptop are still serviceable and useful for web browsing, ‘office work’, and light coding. These machine are too slow to handle tasks like video editing or gaming, but they remain consistent in handling everyday tasks without failing under normal wear and tear.
One of the main reasons that old Thinkpads stand out is their
design philosophy
. They are made with swappable components with the intention of user upgradeability. The battery, RAM, storage drive, keyboard, and even the CPU can be easily replaced. I can open the bottom of my T400 with a regular screwdriver and clean the fan. A battery swap is trivial thanks to a removable pack. No single failure is catastrophic because there’s a straightforward path to replacement or repair.
The
build quality
greatly contributes to old Thinkpads robustness. They are made with a sturdy chassis with plastic and magnesium alloy elements, giving it a solid feel. The design absorbs bumps and small impacts without major issues. They can easily take accidental knocks and remain fully operational.
Old Thinkpads benefits from an
open ecosystem
. They uses standard PC architecture (x86), so installing various operating systems is easy. On the hardware side, replacement parts are widely available on the secondary market. This broad compatibility keeps the machine relevant long past its original release date. By Taleb’s Lindy Effect, the fact that my T400 can still work well after so many years suggests
it’s likely to remain functional as people have already figured out the ways to significantly extend its lifespan
.
All these factors show how the my Thinkpad is
robust
: it resists sudden failures, and when problems do arise, their are documented way to fit it. Old beat up Thinkpads are Lindy.
Modern MacBooks: High Performance, But Fragile
My MacBook offers exceptional speed and efficiency an order of magnitude more than my Thinkpad. It handles tasks—like video editing or running large LLM’s without breaking a sweat. Under ideal conditions, it’s reliable and powerful.
However, from a Talebian perspective, my MacBook’s design is
fragile
. Most components of the laptop are soldered onto the logic board. If the SSD or RAM fails, there’s no simple replacement option. A single failure in a component of my MacBook can render the entire laptop unusable. The tightly integrated design of modern Apple hardware increases the stakes of any malfunction.
The
repairability
of Apple products is extremely limited. Apple uses proprietary screws and adhesives, and parts are incompatible with third-party replacements. A battery replacement (usually one of the first things that fails in mobile electronics) involves carefully prying out a glued component. Routine maintenance tasks that are straightforward on the Thinkpad can require specialized tools and authorized service for the MacBook. This lack of modularity means the system can easily become bricked from hardware fails from component parts.
Another aspect contributing to the fragility of MacBooks is Apple’s
software control
. Apple’s software updates and security updates to macOS essentially determines how long the MacBook remains safe to use. Once Apple ends official support for a machine the user has to buy a new MacBook or use an increasingly compromised system. Apple hardware uses an arm architecture that cannot ‘dual boot’ Windows or Linux easily. Once macOS support dies for a modern MacBook it becomes obsolete.
While my MacBook is great to use, the machine has a lifespan built into its OS support and cannot recover easily from physical damage. MacBooks are not modular, completely propriet

data.title: Why I don't discuss politics with friends
data.author: shw1n
data.article_summary: 本文解释了作者为何避免与朋友讨论政治。主要原因有三点：首先，大多数人并非持有政治观点，而是属于政治部落，习惯以部落立场代替独立思考；其次，培养独立政治思维非常困难，需要跨学科知识和自我偏见觉察；第三，许多人不愿放弃部落思维，因为部落归属带来关系和情感满足，即使这些关系建立在虚假信息上。人们更愿意通过部落（如朋友、新闻）获取现成观点，而非独立思考，从而导致意识形态对立而非理性讨论。作者认为，尽管克服部落思维是可能的，但大多数人并不愿意这么做。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何看待政治讨论及其影响

不同观点：
• [rebeccaskinner] 认为价值观和伦理是政治讨论的核心，政党的政策反映了不同的价值观和世界观。不同的价值观导致无法在政策上达成一致，因此政治讨论往往变成价值观的碰撞，而不是简单的部落主义。
• [talkingtab] 强调政治的核心应是普通公民的生活条件和民主制度的功能，而不是个人、政党或敏感社会议题。政治讨论应该围绕这些基本问题展开，而不是被其他因素分散注意力。
• [fergie] 主张政治讨论是必要的，因为社会进步依赖于思想交流和集体行动。虽然人们会有不同的优先事项和观点，但尊重和沟通可以弥合分歧。
• [rdegges] 持反对意见，认为有些政治观点和行为会对人造成实际伤害，坚持这些观点的人不值得保持友谊。政治分歧不仅仅是意见不同，而是涉及基本的权利和尊严问题。
• [JKCalhoun] 反对将政治分歧简单归结为部落主义，认为自己的政治立场反映了深思熟虑的信念，而不是盲目追随某个群体。
• [pcblues] 观察到过去十年中，社交媒体的兴起加剧了部落主义，政治讨论变得更具对抗性。
• [jjani] 批评“温和派”一词的误用，认为独立思考不必然导致温和立场，而是产生多样化和务实的观点。
• [simpaticoder] 认为人们不愿质疑自己的信念是因为这过程痛苦，且在当前社会环境中，自我反思可能被视为不利于自身利益。
• [panstromek] 主张关注实际可行的共识和行动，而不是空泛的政治辩论，后者可能带来负面影响。
• [sD4fG_9hJ] 建议通过理解彼此的价值观和经验来进行更有成效的政治讨论。
• [roenxi] 引入成人发展理论，解释社会动态和政治行为，认为大多数人依赖社会信号来判断真相。
• [munificent] 提出人类的“魔法思维”倾向，认为这种倾向在世俗社会中表现为各种形式的“宗教性”行为，包括政治。
• [delichon] 否认独立思考者通常是温和派，认为最独立的思想者往往走向极端。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于政治讨论的本质和目的。一部分人认为政治讨论应围绕实际生活问题展开，另一部分人则认为政治讨论反映了更深层次的价值观冲突。
• 社交媒体和新闻媒体在制造分歧和传播偏见中的角色也被多次提及，许多人认为媒体的偏见和误导信息加剧了政治对立。
• 自我反思和批判性思维的重要性被多次强调，作为解决政治分歧和促进社会进步的手段。
• 友谊和关系的价值也被讨论，一些人认为政治分歧不应影响个人关系，而另一些人则认为严重的政治分歧可以破坏关系。

这些观点展示了政治讨论的复杂性和多面性，涉及价值观、媒体影响、心理因素和社会结构等多个方面。

43559605.article_content:
Why I don't discuss politics with friends
March 2025
For as much as I enjoy analyzing politics[1], I'm even more against discussing it with friends. This policy arose from three patterns observed over the years:
Most people don't have political views, they have political
tribes
Developing the political reasoning skills to graduate from tribes to views is incredibly difficult
and the kicker:
Most people don't
want
to graduate from tribes to views
Often when someone asks "who did you vote for", what they're actually doing is verifying your adherence to group culture, like a congregation member asking "you believe in god, right?" loudly in church.
The insidious nature of this question comes from the false representation as earnest, intellectual discourse. Many who ask it may truly believe they’re engaging earnestly, but their responses quickly reveal an angle more akin to religious police.
Most vulnerable to this behavior are the intellectually honest + socially clueless, who engage in good faith, unaware of the pending social ambush.
Why does this happen?
I think there are two main reasons, the first being the sheer intellectual difficulty of crafting an informed political view leads people to tribalism out of convenience.
Being informed is tough
To have an informed view on any given issue, one needs to:
understand economics, game theory, philosophy, sales, business, military strategy, geopolitics, sociology, history, and more
be able to understand and empathize with the various (and often opposing) groups involved in a topic
detect and ignore their own bias
How can you prioritize limited resources with deadly consequences without understanding utilitarianism vs deontology (i.e. the trolly problem)?
Understand China-US relations without understanding communism vs capitalism, the fear of tyranny vs the threat of invasion, or how and where computer chips are made?
How military power dictates realities, economies affect happiness, or how frivolous lawsuits can protect consumers? How companies are built, how elections are won, or the role nuclear families and 30-year fixed mortgages play in America?
And even with all this knowledge, can you empathize with both sides of common issues -- the poor renter vs underwater landlord? The tired worker vs strugglingbusiness owner? Rich vs poor, immigrant vs legacy, parent vs child -- the list goes on.
Each side has both villains and victims. Both landlords and renters can be perpetrators and innocent. Both workers and business owners can be exploited and stolen from.
Yet most people can only identify with one narrative, usually one they've experienced or have a connection to. To acquire, then properly apply this knowledge while honestly detecting your own bias is such an undertaking it's no wonder I only know one or two people capable of it[2].
So it's no surprise humans resort to what’s worked for thousands of years: find our tribe and rep their beliefs, hard.[3]
note: this graph is not meant to imply only moderates are independent thinkers, but was a visual representation of Paul Graham’s “The Two Kinds of Moderate”. Each dot represents the
average
of a person’s
entire
collection of views (which could be spread out)
—
imo the hump could absolutely be shifted left or right, but the likelihood of someone independently agreeing with all of “the left” or “the right’s” views is unlikely given some percentage of each group’s stances are arbitrary
Why spend weeks or months reading when we can outsource this work to the tribe? It can be our friends, church, or even our favorite news station. Throughout history this method has been so successful we've literally evolved to do it. It's why we laugh when others laugh, run when others start running, want things because others want them -- tribalism is built-in.
But when you acquire opinions in bulk like this, suddenly you don’t have a reasoned view, you have an ideology. Your opinions on sex can predict your opinions on taxation [17]. And it removes the ability to discourse because suddenly learning is replaced with cheering, discovery replaced with winning/losing.
Despite this inherent weakness, overcoming tribalism to improve our reasoning is still doable,
if
we desire. But this brings us to the second, darker reality:
Most people don't
want
to graduate from tribalism.
People don't want to leave the tribe
By far, relationships determine the happiness of ones life, and relationships are not beholden to truth. In fact, they are very commonly built on the opposite.
Whether a boss' reprimands are deserved or not, employees bond over a common enemy. Entire groups form on the basis of beliefs, false or otherwise. We have a word for this: “religion".
Despite organized religion dropping in attendance, religious patterns of behavior are still everywhere, just adapted to a secular world.
Health, exercise, politics, work, self-improvement -- these are all things I've seen friends employ their religious muscle into, across all spectrums and pol
