不同观点：
• [rebeccaskinner] 认为价值观和伦理是政治讨论的核心，政党的政策反映了不同的价值观和世界观。不同的价值观导致无法在政策上达成一致，因此政治讨论往往变成价值观的碰撞，而不是简单的部落主义。
• [talkingtab] 强调政治的核心应是普通公民的生活条件和民主制度的功能，而不是个人、政党或敏感社会议题。政治讨论应该围绕这些基本问题展开，而不是被其他因素分散注意力。
• [fergie] 主张政治讨论是必要的，因为社会进步依赖于思想交流和集体行动。虽然人们会有不同的优先事项和观点，但尊重和沟通可以弥合分歧。
• [rdegges] 持反对意见，认为有些政治观点和行为会对人造成实际伤害，坚持这些观点的人不值得保持友谊。政治分歧不仅仅是意见不同，而是涉及基本的权利和尊严问题。
• [JKCalhoun] 反对将政治分歧简单归结为部落主义，认为自己的政治立场反映了深思熟虑的信念，而不是盲目追随某个群体。
• [pcblues] 观察到过去十年中，社交媒体的兴起加剧了部落主义，政治讨论变得更具对抗性。
• [jjani] 批评“温和派”一词的误用，认为独立思考不必然导致温和立场，而是产生多样化和务实的观点。
• [simpaticoder] 认为人们不愿质疑自己的信念是因为这过程痛苦，且在当前社会环境中，自我反思可能被视为不利于自身利益。
• [panstromek] 主张关注实际可行的共识和行动，而不是空泛的政治辩论，后者可能带来负面影响。
• [sD4fG_9hJ] 建议通过理解彼此的价值观和经验来进行更有成效的政治讨论。
• [roenxi] 引入成人发展理论，解释社会动态和政治行为，认为大多数人依赖社会信号来判断真相。
• [munificent] 提出人类的“魔法思维”倾向，认为这种倾向在世俗社会中表现为各种形式的“宗教性”行为，包括政治。
• [delichon] 否认独立思考者通常是温和派，认为最独立的思想者往往走向极端。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于政治讨论的本质和目的。一部分人认为政治讨论应围绕实际生活问题展开，另一部分人则认为政治讨论反映了更深层次的价值观冲突。
• 社交媒体和新闻媒体在制造分歧和传播偏见中的角色也被多次提及，许多人认为媒体的偏见和误导信息加剧了政治对立。
• 自我反思和批判性思维的重要性被多次强调，作为解决政治分歧和促进社会进步的手段。
• 友谊和关系的价值也被讨论，一些人认为政治分歧不应影响个人关系，而另一些人则认为严重的政治分歧可以破坏关系。

这些观点展示了政治讨论的复杂性和多面性，涉及价值观、媒体影响、心理因素和社会结构等多个方面。

data.title: Interview Coder is an invisible AI for technical interviews
data.author: swisspol
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一次重大的技术面试工具更新，重点推出"Interview Coder"——一款用于技术面试的隐形人工智能工具。该工具能够在Zoom等视频会议中，面试官观看求职者屏幕时不显眼地提供帮助，避免被察觉。文章还提到对Leetcode等传统刷题方式的不满，暗示该工具可能是一种更有效的准备面试方式。工具支持Mac和Windows系统下载。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：技术面试中AI工具的使用及其影响

不同观点：
• **gcp123**：认为技术面试中过度注重算法问题与实际工作不符，他们的团队已经取消了算法问题，改为在实际代码库中进行结对编程，并允许访问Google/文档/AI。他们关注候选人是否能通过问题、提问澄清问题、导航不熟悉的代码以及知道何时使用工具。他们认为AI工具只是暴露了面试过程的缺陷，而不是破坏它。

• **danielvaughn**：采用非结构化面试方法，通过一小时的随意交谈来评估候选人的知识深度和兴趣。这种方法被认为能有效避免AI工具的影响，并能更全面地了解候选人。

• **sbuttgereit**：质疑AI工具是否允许候选人进行“欺诈”，认为这种工具可能涉及道德欺诈问题，尽管不一定达到法律欺诈的程度。

• **MOARDONGZPLZ**：主张所有面试环节都应面对面进行，认为这样可以更好地评估候选人的真实能力，尤其是编码部分。

• **Ozzie_osman**：同意LeetCode等工具测试的技能与实际工作不符，但认为AI工具仍然破坏了非LeetCode类型的面试，如系统设计和实际编码面试。他们认为无论是公司还是候选人，使用欺骗手段都是错误的。

• **18172828286177**：对回归到现场面试表示不满，认为这样会浪费时间和精力。

• **exrhizo**：建议不要禁止AI工具，而是观察候选人如何使用它，以及他们是否能理解AI的回答，评估他们的提示质量和思维能力。

• **jlcases**：提出应用MECE原则（互斥且 collectively exhaustive）来改进AI在复杂任务中的表现，从而更好地评估候选人的知识深度和广度。

• **bilsbie**：提出一个基于推荐的招聘平台想法，推荐人需下注金钱和声誉，如果被推荐人在六个月内被解雇，推荐人将失去这些。

• **ErikAugust**：指出行业对AI的分歧，一些公司不允许在面试中使用AI，但同时在日常工作中却要求使用它，认为AI最终会胜出。

• **CSMastermind**：告诉候选人可以在面试中使用AI，认为这不会改变评价的本质。

• **poincaredisk**：认为这种工具会导致面试只能在现场进行，以避免作弊。

• **siva7**：认为技术面试不应远程进行，最好是通过技术谈话或短对的开发任务来评估候选人，这样即使使用AI工具也很难伪造。

• **koliber**：提出通过观察候选人的眼神和回答的节奏来判断是否使用AI工具，认为行为不自然是一个明显标志。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于AI工具是否破坏了技术面试的公平性和有效性。
• 不同面试方法的有效性被多次提及，包括面对面、结对编程和非结构化面试。
• 对AI工具的伦理性和其在技术面试中的角色存在不同看法。
• 一些评论者认为AI工具只是暴露了面试过程的固有缺陷，而不是造成这些问题的原因。

data.title: World's largest wildlife crossing reaches critical milestone. Now what?
data.author: Stratoscope
data.article_summary: The Wallis Annenberg Wildlife Crossing project in Agoura Hills reached a major milestone as 6,000 cubic yards of specially manufactured soil were added to the structure. This soil, designed to mimic native soils using sand, silt, clay, compost, and local fungi, will support the growth of native plants. The project, expected to be completed by the end of 2026, aims to reconnect fragmented habitats for wildlife, like the famous cougar P-22, over the 101 Freeway. Despite delays due to heavy rains, the first stage, involving seeding and planting native shrubs, will finish this summer. The second stage includes burying utility lines and creating additional acres of habitat to blend the crossing with surrounding hills. Officials and scientists celebrated the soil placement as a key step in addressing habitat fragmentation caused by human development.
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国跨公路野生动物通道项目的必要性、建设时间、设计选择及其实际效果

不同观点：
• WillAdams支持在美国各地区建立类似的野生动物通道，并建议在每个区域中心设立无道路的大型荒野保护区。他引用了一个具体案例来支持他的观点。
• OtherShrezzing同意该项目，但质疑为什么要花费4-6年时间来建造一座相对较小的桥，特别是还需要几个月的完全道路封闭。
• kibwen认为道路对景观是毁灭性的破坏，支持尽可能多地掩埋道路，并提出一个长期目标。
• LinuxBender提议将所有人类基础设施转入地下，以恢复地球表面的自然状态，并认为这可以解决气候变化问题，减少电力负荷。
• jvdvegt质疑该项目是否是最大的野生动物通道，并提供了一个50x150米的通道案例作为比较。
• teekert质疑为什么选择桥梁而不是隧道，认为这样可以保持景观的完整性。
• jkuria开玩笑地表示期待的是关于马赛马拉/塞伦盖蒂的野生动物 crossing，而非当前讨论的公路项目。
• zoklet-enjoyer与OtherShrezzing类似，关注项目为何耗时如此之长。
• recursive对这类野生动物通道的实际效果表示怀疑。
• thimkerbell认为标题是点击诱饵。
• pizlonator讽刺地建议不如建这些东西而不是住房。
• jamra担心野生动物通道建在学校旁边可能带来的安全问题，特别是对孩子的威胁。

补充讨论：
• 有人关注项目的时间和效率问题，认为建设时间过长。
• 有人质疑项目的规模和设计选择，如为什么选择桥梁而不是隧道。
• 对野生动物通道的实际效果存在怀疑。
• 讨论中存在讽刺和幽默成分，如期待非洲的野生动物 crossing 和建议建通道而非住房。
• 对项目可能带来的安全问题表示担忧，特别是涉及儿童时。

Soil flows up a conveyor belt 60 feet to the top of the Wallis Annenberg Wildlife Crossing in Agoura Hills on Monday.
(Al Seib / For The Times)
Monday was momentous for the
Wallis Annenberg Wildlife Crossing
although it still looked like a bridge to nowhere from the 101 Freeway, where more than 300,000 vehicles stream endlessly every day.
Nearly three years after the project began, the critical milestone was visible only to the government officials, scientists and longtime supporters who climbed to the top: soil.
And not just
any
soil. Over the next few days they'll be adding 6,000 cubic yards of specially manufactured soil to cover the crossing, a mix of sand, silt and clay inoculated with a bit of compost and hyperlocal mycorrhizal fungi, carefully designed and tested to mimic the biological makeup of native soils around the site.
The plan is to add 6,000 cubic yards of soil, contoured at different depths, to the top of the Wallis Annenberg Wildlife Crossing.
(Al Seib / For The Times)
Adding soil is a big deal because it means we're nearing the end of Stage 1, when the top is seeded and then planted with native shrubs and perennials, work that should be completed this summer, said Robert Rock, chief executive of Chicago-based Rock Design Associates and the landscape architect overseeing the project.
Advertisement
Advertisement
Advertisement
But we're still a ways from completion, now scheduled for the end of 2026, about a year later than initially planned due to delays from the heavy rains in 2022 and 2023.
Stage 2, the final phase, will connect the structure to the hills at the north and south so that wildlife, like
L.A.’s famous, ill-fated cougar, P-22,
can use it. That stage will start with burying utility lines along a section of Agoura Road, south of the crossing, and moving water lines for recycled water used for irrigation.
Read more:
Saving the next P-22 starts with a million ‘hyperlocal’ seeds and a bare-bones nursery
Late in 2025 or early 2026, Agoura Road will be closed for a few months so the roadway can be covered with a tunnel and lots of soil collected from the Malibu Lake area. The goal is to create natural slopes off the crossing — an additional 12 acres of space that will be planted with native shrubs, perennials, grasses and trees to make the crossing blend as much as possible with the surrounding hills.
Beth Pratt, left, California Regional executive director of the National Wildlife Federation, Penny Sylvester, middle, mayor of Agoura Hills, and Jeremy Wolf, right, Agoura Hills mayor pro tem, giggle as they throw the first soil onto the top of the Wallis Annenberg Wildlife Crossing in Agoura Hills.
(Al Seib / For The Times)
"Basically they're restoring the mountain to what it once was, so wildlife won’t even know they’re crossing the freeway," said Jeremy Wolf, mayor pro tem of Agoura Hills, who was among several government officials, scientists and longtime advocates who came to celebrate the soil's arrival on Monday.
Advertisement
Advertisement
Advertisement
"Humans created this problem," Wolf said in an interview. "We've created islands of habitat fragmentation with our roadways and housing encroaching deeper and deeper into the wild urban interface, and now we're fixing this problem by using human ingenuity for good purposes."
Beth Pratt, California regional executive director of the National Wildlife Federation, right, shows off her P-22 cougar sweater in celebration with Robert Rock, the landscape architect overseeing construction of the Wallis Annenberg Wildlife Crossing, as soil finally begins to flow onto the crossing.
(Al Seib / For The Times)
There has been plenty of ingenuity and innovation along the way and lots of attention to detail. For instance, even before construction began in 2022, the project built a nursery and sent horticulturists combing the hills around the site to collect about 1 million seeds from around 30 native plant species. Those seeds were planted and have been nurtured into 1-gallon pots.
Mycologists (biologists who study fungi) collected beneficial mycorrhizal fungi and other microbes from the area to inoculate the soil used to grow the plants, and cover the top of the structure.
They also tested what native seeds best interacted with that fungi, and chose four to sow as a cover crop before adding the plants to help "jump-start" beneficial fungi growth in the soil, which helps plants access the nutrients and water they need to thrive. Those seeds will be sown later this month, Rock said:
golden yarrow
(
Eriophyllum confertiflorum)
,
California poppy
(
Eschscholzia californica
)
,
giant wildrye
(
Elymus condensatus)
and
Santa Barbara milk vetch
(
Astragalus tric

data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了Ira Glass的《This American Life》广播节目的哲学与故事叙述方式。Glass认为，新闻往往缺乏亚里士多德所定义的故事 essential element：情节。通过情节，即使是日常故事也能吸引听众，让他们持续关注。在当今信息碎片化和注意力短暂的时代，拥有情节的故事能帮助观众克服对政治和文化问题的先入为主的看法。Glass以2019年11月15日的“The Out Crowd”为例，该集聚焦特朗普政府的“留在墨西哥”政策对寻求庇护者的影响，通过九岁洪都拉斯难民Darwin的故事，使听众更关注人性的层面。尽管该节目有过一次重大失误，但总体上成功地通过叙述个人故事吸引了大量听众。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：媒体中的事实与故事讲述之间的张力，以及事实核查的重要性与挑战

不同观点：
• Isamu认为，某些节目应被视为“故事时间”而非新闻报道，观众应清楚不能将其视为事实；同时，对比Tucker Carlson的节目，指出其以意见形式播出，观众可能误以为事实，并通过法律案例说明Carlson如何规避事实陈述的责任。
• gcp123强调故事叙述在媒体中的影响力，尤其是This American Life（TAL）节目中的故事模板对制作人的吸引力，同时指出Daisey事件暴露了追求情感冲击和叙事优雅可能导致的危险，即激励不实信息。
• otterley认为犯错是人之常情，关键在于犯错后的反应，称赞Ira及其团队在意识到错误后采取了正确措施。
• pards引用了TAL的“Mr. Daisey and the Apple Factory”事件，指出该节目在广受欢迎的同时存在大量虚构细节，并在事后进行了更正。
• glenstein提到Daisey的辩解类似于Hasan Minhaj的“情感真相”，认为这种放弃客观现实的做法非常危险。
• kjellsbells举例New York Times的Caliphate podcast系列，指出其同样存在叙事虚构的问题，并附上更正声明链接。
• blindriver认为现代社会不再重视事实，人们只关心信息是否符合自己的情绪，建议教导下一代不要轻信网络信息。
• didgetmaster指出争议性问题往往有两面的事实， biased的故事通常只关注一面，而忽略另一面，事实核查者很少指出明显的遗漏。
• g42gregory强调自行事实核查的重要性，建议阅读原始文件和法庭报告等。
• femiagbabiaka认为许多虚构的叙述服务于美国国务院的谈话要点，并指出主流媒体在其他国际问题上的类似报道模式。
• throwaway81523批评文章过于冗长，建议直接陈述事实，并总结TAL的“Mr. Daisey and the Apple Factory”事件的错误及事后谨慎态度。
• cantaloupes认为文章作者过于自负和傲慢。
• cle指出事实核查存在巨大缺口，媒体容易通过呈现完全真实的事实但暗示错误的因果关系来误导观众，并强调情感背景使事实核查更加复杂。
• spaceisballer提到《The Lifespan of a Fact》一书，探讨事实核查与故事叙述之间的界限问题。
• croes认为人们被故事吸引而非事实，情感叙事往往胜过无故事的事实，这是 populism 成功的原因之一。

补充讨论：
• 评论中多次提到This American Life和Mike Daisey事件，作为故事叙述和事实核查失败的典型案例。
• 讨论中涉及现代媒体对事实的处理方式，包括情感叙事、 biased报道和事实核查的不足。
• 有评论指出 populism 和广告策略中的情感销售手法，说明人们对事实的忽视和对情感的依赖。
• 强调自行事实核查和批判性思维的重要性，建议从第一手资料获取信息。

On the Episode That Changed Ira Glass’s
This American Life
Forever
Or, On the Importance of Fact-Checking
via Avid Reader Press
By
Steve Oney
March 31, 2025
The philosophy that animates Ira Glass’s
This American Life
can be summed up by a simple come on: “Let me tell you a story.” News, almost by definition, rarely conforms to what Aristotle deemed the essential element of storytelling: plot. It consists of dispatches from geographically disparate locales and varying worlds (politics, foreign affairs, finance, sports), and it doesn’t adhere to a scenario.
Article continues after advertisement
Remove Ads
Of late, the proliferation of offerings from online outlets has increased choices while fragmenting audiences, creating an age of hot takes and short attention spans. It’s hard to get consumers of TV and radio news to stay tuned. “Having a plot is a way to make people stick around and provide something that feels satisfying,” Ira Glass noted. “That’s the thing about it that’s helpful. If you have a plot, the story can be mundane. It can be incredibly everyday. But people just want to find out what’s gonna happen, and they’ll hang around.”
Not only this, but plot—or narrative, as its sometimes more grandly called—offers an antidote to the political and cultural polarization changing audience habits. As Glass put it: “The primary problem you have in doing a story about any of the big, emotional issues of our time—was the election stolen, does the vaccine work, what to think of Donald Trump, climate change—is that everybody already knows what they think. If you start any story, everybody’s like, ‘Yeah, yeah, I know.’ There’s an enormous hurdle to get over to get people to listen past even the first thirty-five seconds. What do you do? By having characters, scenes, and surprising moments and just letting the thing unfold, you can catch people up in the lives of the people you’re documenting. And then they’ll keep listening to hear how things work out.”
The apotheosis of the
This American Life
approach is its November 15, 2019, episode, “The Out Crowd,” winner of the inaugural Pulitzer Prize for audio journalism. When the staff of
TAL
began to put together this show, which focuses on how the Trump administration’s Remain in Mexico policy affected asylum seekers trying to cross into the United States, the basic facts of the matter were already familiar. “We knew this had gotten coverage in the
Wall Street Journal
, the
New York Times
, the
Washington Post
, and on the networks,” recalled Glass. “It’s out there—if you follow this. But all of the stories felt academic.” The goal was to capture the human dimensions of a policy that had stranded thousands in desolate shelters deemed unsafe by the US State Department.
“The Out Crowd” opens with a fourteen-minute prologue reported from a tent city in Matamoros, Mexico, just across the Rio Grande from Brownsville, Texas. In it, Glass introduces listeners to an unlikely protagonist—a nine-year-old Honduran refugee named Darwin who along with his mother is hoping to get to America. “I feel like if you said at the beginning that this was a show about immigration, nobody would listen,” said Glass. “The fact that the first few minutes of the show can just be a portrait of this completely charming kid, everybody’s favorite kid—you wanna hear more. Then you pull the camera back. Then you reveal: OK. Here’s what the show is about today.”
Article continues after advertisement
Remove Ads

This American Life
. It has also resulted in one devastating misfire.

Los
Angeles Times

TAL

data.title: Scientists witness living plant cells generate cellulose and form cell walls
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: Rutgers大学的研究团队首次通过显微技术实时观察到活体植物细胞生成纤维素并形成细胞壁的过程。纤维素是由细胞膜上的酶复合物合成，并自组装成微纤丝网络，构成细胞壁的主要支架。这一突破性发现发表在《Science Advances》期刊上，为增强植物耐受性、提高粮食产量及开发低成本生物燃料提供了新思路。研究还揭示了纤维素形成的复杂网络如何通过简单的物理机制如扩散和自组织形成，对植物学基础研究有重要贡献。该研究历时六年，涉及多学科合作，未来可能应用于改进纺织品、生物降解塑料及新医疗产品等领域。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI在艺术渲染和科学研究中的应用

不同观点：
• [whoiscroberts] 认为AI使得制作艺术渲染图的工作变得更容易，暗示AI技术在艺术领域的应用带来了效率提升和简化。这里强调了AI对工作流程的改进，但没有深入讨论技术细节。

• [rashkov] 对文章中提到的科学研究更感兴趣，特别是如何通过AI发现与纤维素合成相关的基因。他提出了具体的技术问题，即通过敲除可能的候选基因并进行图像分析来研究基因功能，关注的是AI在科学研究中的实际应用和具体操作方法。

补充讨论：
• [whoiscroberts] 的评论侧重于AI在艺术和设计领域的简化作用，认为AI降低了制作高质量图像的难度。

• [rashkov] 的评论则深入探讨了AI在生物学研究中的潜力，特别是通过基因敲除和图像分析来推进科学发现，显示出对技术细节和科学方法的关注。

• 争议焦点：两者之间的讨论焦点并不直接对立，但可以看出他们对AI应用的关注点不同。一人关注艺术渲染的简便性，另一人则关注科学研究的精确性和技术细节。这反映了AI技术在不同领域应用时的不同影响和关注方向。

Scientists witness living plant cells generate cellulose and form cell walls for the first time
by
Rutgers University
Artistic rendering of cellulose regenerating on a plant protoplast cell surface with zoomed out view. Cellulose is synthesized by plasma membrane-bound enzyme complexes (green) and assembles into a microfibril network (brown), forming the main scaffold for the cell wall. Credit: Ehsan Faridi/ Inmywork Studio/ Chundawat, Lee and Lam Labs
In a groundbreaking study on the synthesis of cellulose—a major constituent of all plant cell walls—a team of Rutgers University-New Brunswick researchers have captured images of the microscopic process of cell-wall building continuously over 24 hours with living plant cells, providing critical insights that may lead to the development of more robust plants for increased food and lower-cost biofuels production.
The discovery,
published
in the journal
Science Advances
, reveals a
dynamic process
never seen before and may provide practical applications for everyday products derived from plants, including enhanced textiles, biofuels, biodegradable plastics, and new medical products.
The research is also expected to contribute to the fundamental knowledge while providing a new understanding of the formation of cell walls, the scientists said.
It represents over six years of effort and collaboration among three laboratories from differing but complementary academic disciplines at Rutgers: the School of Arts and Sciences, the School of Engineering, and the School of Environmental and Biological Sciences.
A time-lapse video showing Arabidopsis cells generate cellulose fibrils. Credit: Lee Lab/Rutgers University
"This work is the first direct visualization of how
cellulose
synthesizes and self-assembles into a dense fibril network on a plant cell surface, since Robert Hook's first microscopic observation of cell walls in 1667," said Sang-Hyuk Lee, an associate professor in the Department of Physics and Astronomy and an author of the study.
"This study also provides entirely new insights into how simple, basic physical mechanisms such as diffusion and self-organization may lead to the formation of complex cellulose networks in cells."
The microscope-generated video images show protoplasts—cells with their walls removed—of cabbage's cousin, the flowering plant Arabidopsis, chaotically sprouting filaments of cellulose fibers that gradually self-assemble into a complex network on the outer cell surface.
"I was very surprised by the emergence of ordered structures out of the chaotic dance of molecules when I first saw these video images," said Lee, who is also a faculty member at the Institute for Quantitative Biomedicine. "I thought plant cellulose would be made in a lot more of an organized fashion, as depicted in classical biology textbooks."
Cellulose is the most abundant biopolymer—
large molecules
naturally produced by living organisms—on Earth. A carbohydrate that is the primary structural component of plant cell walls, cellulose is widely used in industry to make a range of products, including paper and clothing. It is also used in filtration, trapping large particles more effectively and enhancing flow, and as a thickening agent in foods such as yogurt and ice cream.
"This discovery opens the door for researchers to begin dissecting the genes that could play various roles for cellulose biosynthesis in the plant," said Eric Lam, a Distinguished Professor in the Department of Plant Biology in Rutgers School of Environmental and Biological Sciences and an author of the study.
"The knowledge gained from these future studies will provide new clues for approaches to design better plants for
carbon capture
, improve tolerance to all kinds of environmental stresses, from drought to disease, and optimize second-generation cellulosic biofuels production."

data.title: Protoplanetary Disks Are Smaller Than Expected
data.author: JPLeRouzic
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了原行星盘的最新研究成果，发现这些盘的尺寸通常比之前认为的要小。利用ALMA望远镜的数据，天文学家对距离地球400光年的Lupus星云中的原行星盘进行了高分辨率观测，结果显示大多数盘比太阳系的范围小，且缺乏明显的结构如缝隙和环。这意味着多数恒星可能并不拥有巨行星，而小盘更适合形成超级地球。研究还指出，像太阳这样较大质量的恒星才可能拥有足够大的原行星盘以形成木星和土星等巨行星。这些发现改变了对行星形成环境的传统看法，并将原行星盘与已观测到的系外行星群体联系起来。

- 观察偏差对科学研究结果的影响程度，尤其是在评估恒星分布和生命普遍性问题上，是否被充分认识和纠正。

Protoplanetary Disks Are Smaller Than Expected
by
Paul Gilster
|
Apr 4, 2025
|
Exoplanetary Science
|
0 comments
In astronomy, the first thing you see may be the least typical. A case in point: ‘Hot Jupiters.’ A few prescient souls, among them Buzz Aldrin and John Barnes in their novel
Encounter with Tiber
, speculated about gas giants that survived incredibly tight orbits around their star, and when asked about this in the 1990s, Greg Matloff ran the numbers and confirmed to his surprise that there was a theoretical case for their existence.  Let me quote Matloff on this:
Although I was initially very skeptical since then-standard models of solar system formation seemed to rule out such a possibility, I searched through the literature and located the appropriate equation (Jastrow and Rasool, 1965)….To my amazement, Buzz was correct. The planet’s atmosphere is stable for billions of years. Since I was at the time working as a consultant and adjunct professor, I did not challenge the existing physical paradigm by submitting my results to a mainstream journal. Since “Hot Jupiters” were discovered shortly before the novel was published, I am now credited with predicting the existence of such worlds.
51 Pegasi b made the case for ‘hot Jupiters’ convincingly in 1995, and we also know that the reason we began finding these planets was that our best methods for detecting exoplanets in the mid-1990s involved radial velocity and transit  measurements, both of which are most effective when dealing with large planets in close orbits. As best I can determine, current estimates find a scant ~0.5–1% of these planets around F-, G-, or K-class stars. The rarity of hot Jupiters like TOI-4201b underlines how rare these objects are around M-dwarfs.
Observational bias can be a tricky thing. So is something of the same phenomenon occurring in our study of how planets form? Protoplanetary disks are extensively studied, some of them showing what appear to be planets in their early stages of formation. As I’ve read studies about disks like those at TW Hydrae and HL Tauri, I’ve always assumed that they were massive. In some cases they extend far beyond our Solar System’s outer reaches. But now we have a new study making a strong case that disks like these are not typical.
The work in question involved data from ALMA, the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array. It comprises data from observations from 2023 and 2024 at resolutions of 0.030 arcsecond, along with somewhat higher resolution archival data to produce a high resolution survey of an entire star-forming region. The imaging takes in all known protoplanetary disks around young stars in the Lupus star forming region, some 400 light years from Earth.
The results indicate how much we have to learn about protoplanetary disks. The smallest disk comes to only 0.6 astronomical units in radius, which means it is smaller than the Earth’s orbit. The researchers also learned that the kind of features that point to planets in formation do not occur in smaller disks. Thus lead author Osmar M. Guerra-Alvarado (Leiden University, The Netherlands):
“These results completely change our view of what a ‘typical’ protoplanetary disc looks like. Only the brightest discs which are the easiest to observe show large-scale gaps, whereas compact discs without such substructures are actually much more common.”
Image:
Images of 73 protoplanetary discs in the Lupus star forming region (two of the images contain binary stars). Only a fraction of the discs extend beyond the orbit of Neptune, when compared to our own Solar System. Most of the observed discs are small and show no structures like gaps and rings. (c) Guerra-Alvarado et al.
Adds Leiden colleague Nienke van der Marel:
“The discovery that the majority of the small discs do not show gaps, implies that the majority of stars do not host giant planets. This is consistent with what we see in exoplanet populations around full-grown stars. These observations link the disc population directly to the exoplanet population.”
The smaller protoplanetary disks are found around stars massing between 10 and 50 percent of the mass of the Sun. While disks like these do not appear optimum for the formation of gas giants, they may be fertile breeding ground for super-Earths, with most of the dust located close to the host star. Given this context, our own Solar System may have been formed from a more massive protoplanetary disk large enough to produce a Jupiter and a Saturn.
Image:
This is an artist’s impression of a young star surrounded by a protoplanetary disc in which planets are forming. Using ALMA’s 15-kilometre baseline astronomers were able to make the first detailed image of a protoplanetary disc, which revealed the complex structure of the disc. Concentric rings of gas, with gaps indicating planet formation, are visible in this artist’s impression and were predicted by computer simulations. Now these structures have been observed by ALMA for the first

data.title: AdNauseam: Clicking ads so you don't have to
data.author: thunderbong
data.article_summary: AdNauseam是一款浏览器扩展，通过自动点击被屏蔽的广告，扰乱广告网络的用户追踪和监控。基于uBlock Origin，它模拟大量点击，使广告商的数据收集失效，保护用户隐私。该工具旨在表达对忽视隐私的广告网络的不满，并采用混淆策略，使用户能够反抗单方面的监控。AdNauseam属于通过技术手段实现伦理和政治目标的系统，类似于TrackMeNot，旨在打破追踪与被追踪者之间的力量平衡。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对广告模式、广告拦截工具的看法及相关法律问题

不同观点：
• [Nifty3929] 认为用户更倾向于看到高价值、精准投放的广告，而不是低价值、无关的广告。他指出当前的广告模式是通过广告支持内容免费消费，如果广告精准度高，用户只需看少量广告。虽然他不喜欢被追踪，但承认这是现实，并希望减少带有恶意设计（dark-pattern）的广告。

• [cj] 提出警告，随意点击网页上的广告可能会被标记为机器人或异常行为，从而导致用户看到更多验证码或类似安全措施。这暗示了对使用广告拦截或反广告工具可能带来的负面影响。

• [beejiu] 认为在英国使用类似AdNauseam的工具可能是违法的，指出了在某些国家使用广告拦截工具的法律风险。

• [nvr219] 关注具体的广告问题，询问如何去除"admiral"弹出广告，显示出用户对实际广告困扰的关注，而非对广告模式的广泛讨论。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是广告精准投放与用户隐私之间的矛盾。虽然一些用户愿意接受精准广告以减少广告数量，但他们仍对隐私追踪感到不安。
• 另一个值得注意的点是使用广告拦截工具可能引发的技术问题（如被标记为异常行为）和法律问题（如在某些国家的合法性）。
• 具体广告问题（如"admiral"弹出广告）显示了用户对实际广告体验的困扰，这可能推动他们寻找技术解决方案。

As online advertising becomes ever more ubiquitous and unsanctioned,
AdNauseam works to complete the cycle by automating ad clicks universally
and blindly on behalf of its users. Built atop uBlock Origin, AdNauseam
quietly clicks on every blocked ad, registering a visit on ad networks'
databases. As the collected data gathered shows an omnivorous click-stream, user
tracking, targeting and surveillance become futile. Read more about AdNauseam in this
paper
.
AdNauseam
is a free browser extension
designed to obfuscate browsing data and protect users from tracking by advertising networks.
At the same time, AdNauseam serves
as a means of amplifying users' discontent with advertising networks
that disregard privacy and facilitate bulk surveillance agendas.
AdNauseam joins a broader class of technical systems that attempt to serve
ethical, political, and expressive ends. In light of the industry's
failure
to self-regulate or otherwise address the excesses of network tracking, AdNauseam
allows individual users to take matters into their own hands, fighting
back against unilateral surveillance. Taken in this light, the software
follows an approach similar to that of
TrackMeNot
,
employing obfuscation as a strategy to shift the balance of power between
the trackers and the tracked. For further information on this approach,
please see this
paper
.

data.article_summary: 一项由爱丁堡大学主导的大型国际调查发现，饮食改变可能帮助缓解子宫内膜异位症的疼痛。研究涉及2,599人，结果显示，45%停止摄入谷蛋白和乳制品的女性报告疼痛有所减轻，43%减少咖啡因摄入的女性也感到疼痛缓解，53%减少饮酒的女性同样表示疼痛减少。研究人员认为，这些饮食调整可能通过影响肠道细菌和减少炎症发挥作用。尽管这些发现为患者提供了自我管理疼痛的希望，但专家建议在做出饮食改变前应咨询医生，并需要更多大型研究来验证这些效果。子宫内膜异位症影响全球许多女性，但其病因和治疗方法研究不足，通常仅通过手术或激素药物管理症状。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于子宫内膜异位症的症状、治疗困难以及相关的饮食与注意力缺陷多动障碍（ADHD）管理的讨论。

不同观点：
• [bognition] 强调子宫内膜异位症的痛苦及其对女性生活的影响，尤其是与男性医生沟通中的怀疑和症状无效认定问题。她还指出，目前医学界对该疾病了解不足，缺乏有效的治疗手段，这是一种悲剧。

• [goda90] 关注的是如何在患有ADHD的情况下管理和追踪子宫内膜异位症的饮食与疼痛。他提出了一个实际问题，即如何帮助患有ADHD的亲人应对子宫内膜异位症的饮食触发因素，鉴于ADHD可能使追踪和执行这些管理策略变得困难。

• [aziaziazi] 提供了有关子宫内膜异位症疼痛机制的科学解释，指出子宫内膜异位症组织能够生成新的神经细胞并增加现有神经细胞的活跃度，从而导致更严重的疼痛感。同时，提到通过饮食调整控制炎症可能是有效的治疗方向。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是医学界对子宫内膜异位症的认知不足，以及患者在寻求治疗时遭遇的性别偏见和不信任问题。
• 另一个讨论点是患有子宫内膜异位症并同时患有ADHD的患者如何有效地进行饮食和疼痛管理，这涉及到具体的实践建议和支持方案。
• 最后，关于通过饮食调整控制炎症的科学依据也被提出，作为潜在的治疗策略，但尚未被完全验证或广泛应用。

Study believes findings will be ‘tremendously empowering’ for endometriosis sufferers.
Photograph: fizkes/Getty Images/iStockphoto
View image in fullscreen

Photograph: fizkes/Getty Images/iStockphoto
The Observer
Endometriosis
Major endometriosis study reveals impact of gluten, coffee, dairy and alcohol
Edinburgh University report authors say dietary changes could benefit women living with the disease
Victoria Allen
Sat 5 Apr 2025 06.04 EDT
Share
Dietary changes could reduce the pain of endometriosis for half of those living with the disease, a new study suggests. The largest international survey ever conducted on diet and endometriosis, involving 2,599 people, found 45% of those who stopped eating gluten and 45% of those who cut out dairy reported experiencing an improvement in their pain.
When women cut down on coffee or other caffeine in their diet, 43% said their pain was reduced, while 53% of women who cut back on alcohol reported the same.
Philippa Saunders, senior author of the study and professor of reproductive steroids at the University of Edinburgh, said: “It really feels like we are on the cusp of something pretty big with understanding how diet affects endometriosis symptoms.
“It is so important for women if they feel they can do something for themselves to tackle the pain of endometriosis – that is tremendously empowering.”
Endometriosis occurs when cells similar to those in the lining of the womb grow in other parts of the body. It affects one in 10 women of reproductive age in the UK.
However, there is very little research into the causes of the disease or how to treat it – beyond surgery, which is often only a short-term fix, or managing symptoms through hormonal contraceptives like the pill, which many women dislike because of side effects. It takes an average of almost seven years for women to receive a diagnosis of endometriosis due to lack of awareness about the disease.
The new study, led by Edinburgh University and published last week in the American medical Association’s journal JAMA Network Open, asked volunteers about changes to their diet and about dietary supplements used to try to improve their symptoms. Researchers believe that the women who cut out gluten or dairy and reported feeling less pain may have experienced changes in their gut bacteria.
Reducing caffeine may work because it can affect sleep, and pain often feels worse when people are tired. Cutting back on alcoholic drinks is potentially impactful because alcohol has a similar effect on cells to oestrogen – the hormone that fuels endometriosis.
Endometriosis largely causes pain in the pelvic area, which is often worse during periods, but many sufferers report sciatic pain, with others experiencing breast pain or a flu-like joint pain affecting the whole body.
The womb-like tissue of endometriosis is able to grow new nerve cells – the cells that transmit pain sensations – and make existing nerve cells more active. The pain signals this sends to the brain are increased even more by inflammation – an overreaction of the immune system. It is this inflammation that could be tackled by dietary changes, experts believe.
Cutting back on certain foods may reduce bacteria in the gut that powers inflammation. The study found almost 40% of respondents reported reduced pain from endometriosis after cutting out processed food like ready meals, ice-cream and sweets, which are known to alter gut bacteria.
Almost a third of women said their pain improved after cutting out garlic and onion, which could relieve so-called “endo belly” – uncomfortable bloating sufferers can experience.
Experts say people should check with their doctor before making dietary changes. Larger studies, with women randomly assigned to different diets, are still needed to gather compelling evidence on how diet might affect endometriosis, and could include measurements of people’s inflammation and pain.
The Edinburgh study relied on self-reported pain levels and surveyed people from 51 countries, including 1,115 people from the UK.
Francesca Hearn-Yeates, who led the study from the University of Edinburgh, said: “Women are in need of anything that can help with the pain of endometriosis. This condition is so under-researched and there is so much to discover, but there is growing evidence that gut bacteria could play a part in symptoms, and that explains why many women have experimented with changing their diets, and why we have found that this appears to work for many.”
Jo Hanley, specialist adviser for Endometriosis UK, said: “We follow with interest studies on the potential impact and role of diet and nutrition in the management of endometriosis.
“There is a need for more high-quality evidence but I’ve heard many a success story from individuals where dietary changes have led to improved pain, although unfortunately others have reported no improvements.

• [aziaziazi] 提供了有关子宫内膜异位症疼痛机制的科学解释，指出子宫内膜异位症组织能够生成新的神经细胞并增加现有神经细胞的活跃度，从而导致更严重的疼痛感。同时，提到通过饮食调整控制炎症可能是有效的治疗方向。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是医学界对子宫内膜异位症的认知不足，以及患者在寻求治疗时遭遇的性别偏见和不信任问题。
• 另一个讨论点是患有子宫内膜异位症并同时患有ADHD的患者如何有效地进行饮食和疼痛管理，这涉及到具体的实践建议和支持方案。
• 最后，关于通过饮食调整控制炎症的科学依据也被提出，作为潜在的治疗策略，但尚未被完全验证或广泛应用。

data.title: Tariffs Can Help America
data.author: ckcheng
data.article_summary: 文章《关税如何帮助美国》由迈克尔·佩蒂斯撰写，讨论了关税政策的有效性及其历史误解。作者指出，许多人以1930年的斯穆特-霍利关税法失败为例，反对当今的关税政策，但这种比较并不恰当。斯穆特-霍利法失败是因为当时美国生产过剩，而当今美国是消费过剩、储蓄过低。在这种情况下，适度的关税可能反而有助于增加就业和工资，促进经济增长。佩蒂斯认为，关税的效果取决于实施时的经济环境，不能一概而论。当前美国的经济状况与1930年代不同，关税政策可能产生积极效果，而非历史上的负面影响。

U.S. President-elect Donald Trump has promised to implement a suite of aggressive tariffs on American trade partners, including a blanket 20 percent levy on goods from abroad. Although his supporters claim that these tariffs will strengthen U.S. manufacturing and create jobs, critics contend that they will fuel inflation, suppress employment, and perhaps tip the economy into a recession. As a demonstration of what will go wrong, many cite the Smoot-Hawley Tariff Act of 1930, which raised U.S. tariffs across a variety of imports. “Judging by his proposed import tariff policy,” wrote the American Enterprise Institute economist Desmond Lachman, “it is evident that Donald Trump does not remember our country’s disastrous economic experience with the 1930 Smoot-Hawley Trade Act.”
But these claims only show how confused many experts are when it comes to trade—on both sides of the tariff debate. Tariffs are neither a panacea nor necessarily injurious. Their effectiveness, like that of any economic policy intervention, depends on the circumstances under which they are implemented. Smoot-Hawley was a failure at its time, but its failure tells analysts very little about the effect that tariffs would have on the United States today. That is because now, unlike then, the United States is not producing far more than it can consume. Ironically, the history of Smoot-Hawley says a lot more about how tariffs today would affect a country such as China, whose excess production more closely resembles that of the United States in the 1920s than does the United States of now.
Economists weren’t always so mixed up. In his classic 1944 book,
International Currency Experience
, Ragnar Nurkse wrote that “the devaluation of a currency is expansionary in effect if it corrects a previous overvaluation, but deflationary if it makes the currency undervalued.” Tariffs, which are close cousins of currency devaluation, act in the same way. They reduce domestic consumption and force up domestic savings rates. A country with low consumption and excess savings (like the United States in the 1920s or China today) tends to be one with an undervalued currency, in which case tariffs, like currency depreciation, are likely to be deflationary. But in a country with excessively high levels of consumption, like the modern United States, the same policy can be expansionary. Done under current circumstances, in other words, tariffs could increase employment and wages in the United States, raising living standards and growing the economy.
WRONG PLACE, WRONG TIME
For those who don’t remember (or who never had a chance
to see
Ferris Bueller’s Day Off
), the Smoot-Hawley Tariff Act was a controversial law that raised tariffs on over 20,000 goods. Named after its two Republican sponsors, Senator Reed Smoot of Utah and Representative Willis C. Hawley of Oregon, and signed into law by a reluctant President Herbert Hoover on June 17, 1930, it represented the second-highest tariff increase in U.S. history.
Smoot-Hawley was implemented at the beginning of the Great Depression, when countries around the world were already engaged in the currency depreciation, import restrictions, and tariffs that English economist Joan Robinson would later
characterize
as “beggar-my-neighbor” policies. As Robinson explained, these policies expand domestic growth by subsidizing production at the expense of domestic consumption. They do so through many ways, but they all use the resulting trade surpluses to shift the cost of weak demand onto trade partners. Put simply, beggar-my-neighbor policies are designed to prop up one country’s economy at the expense of another, usually by boosting domestic manufacturing at the expense of foreign manufacturing.

data.title: Are porn algorithms feeding a generation of paedophiles – or creating one?
data.author: sandebert
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了网络儿童性虐待图像案件的激增，尤其是在英格兰和威尔士，每月约有850名男性因相关罪行被捕。案例显示，许多人最初因沉迷于色情内容，逐渐被引向更黑暗的网络空间，甚至涉及儿童色情。例如，一位名叫安迪的男子因分享儿童性虐待图像被捕，他声称自己的色情成瘾逐渐升级，最终导致犯罪行为。另一位被捕者马克则表示，他并未意识到自己观看的大量色情内容中包含未成年人的图像。文章指出，随着免费和易访问的网络色情内容激增，越来越多的人，尤其是年轻人，可能因此接触到非法材料。专家警告，极端色情内容可能成为观看儿童性虐待图像的途径，并质疑色情网站是否应对这一趋势负责。文章还提到，如前BBC主持人休·爱德华兹等知名人士也卷入此类案件，显示出问题的普遍性。警方和儿童保护专家正努力应对这一全球性危机，呼吁加强刑罚以遏制相关犯罪。

‘I didn’t start out wanting to see kids’: are porn algorithms feeding a generation of paedophiles – or creating one?
More than 850 men a month are arrested for online child abuse offences in England and Wales. They come from every walk of life: teachers, police officers, doctors, TV presenters. And the numbers are rising every year. How did this happen?
Harriet Grant
Sat 5 Apr 2025 02.00 EDT
Last modified on Sat 5 Apr 2025 05.28 EDT
Share
A
ndy was enjoying a weekend away with his wife when it happened. “My neighbour phoned me and said, ‘The police are in your house. They’re looking for you.’” He didn’t need to wonder why. “You know. You know the reason. I was petrified when I got that call. It wasn’t just the thought of other people knowing what I had done; I also had to face myself, and that is a sick feeling – it is guilt, shame.”
Andy had been watching and sharing images of children being sexually abused for several months before the police appeared at his door. He tried at first to keep it from his wife: “I was afraid she would ask me to leave. I wouldn’t have blamed her if she had.”
When they got home, he told her his story: that a spiralling porn addiction had led him to ever darker places, chatrooms where people talked about sex and porn, and shared images and videos. “That was where someone sent me a picture of a child, in exchange for some porn I sent them.”
I knew I had looked at lots of porn but I genuinely did not think there was anybody underage in there
Unlike Andy, Mark didn’t immediately realise why the police had come for him. “My then wife came in looking worried and said, ‘There are police at the door.’ We were living in a wealthy area, so I thought they were there about some recent burglaries. But then they told me they needed to speak to me alone. They said I was being arrested for having indecent images of children.”
Mark claims he was shellshocked. “I knew I had looked at lots of porn but I genuinely did not think there was anybody underage in there. They said they had found 200 illegal images.” From the outside, Mark was a successful businessman, travelling regularly for work. His arrest was a public humiliation. “There were four of them, with body cameras on, in two cars. They told my boys, ‘Don’t worry, Daddy is just helping us out’ and put me in the back of one of the cars. In the picture the police took that day, I look suicidal.”
In England and Wales,
850 men a month
are arrested for online child abuse offences. They come from every walk of life: teachers, police officers, bus drivers, doctors. Those on the frontline are warning of another alarming trend: a significant shift towards younger offenders among those picked up for watching illegal material.
The arrests are just one metric pointing towards a spiralling global crisis. Last year was the worst on record for instances of online child sexual abuse imagery, with the UK’s
Internet Watch Foundation
acting to remove content from 300,000 web pages
,
each containing at least one, if not hundreds or thousands, of illegal images and videos.
Now, police, charities, lawyers and child protection experts are asking what is driving this tidal wave of offending, and finding one common thread: the explosion over the past 10 to 20 years of free-to-view and easily accessible online pornography. Material so violent it would have been considered highly extreme a generation ago is now readily available on iPads, desktops and the phones in teenagers’ pockets. A growing body of research is beginning to warn of how problematic porn habits can be a pathway into viewing images of children being abused.
I have been writing about the online child abuse crisis for five years. Time and again I have heard warnings from those on the frontline that there is an unambiguous link between the two. Do the sites that profit from porn have questions to answer about this link? Can the connection be broken? And the big question: is the explosion of child abuse imagery online feeding a demand for this material, or creating one?
T
he scale of the problem faced by the police was made clear to the public last year, when former BBC presenter
Huw Edwards was given a suspended sentence
, avoiding jail time, after being found guilty of accessing indecent photographs of children as young as seven. This highlighted the fact that most people –
around eight out of 10
– caught with images of children being sexually abused are not jailed. The National Crime Agency has called for more prison sentences, warning that
up to 830,000 adults in the UK, 1.6% of the population, pose a threat to children
.

data.title: Europe needs its own social media platforms to safeguard sovereignty
data.author: robtherobber
data.article_summary: 文章指出，欧洲的社交媒体生态被美国平台主导，如Meta、Alphabet和X（Twitter），导致欧洲在数字领域的自主权受到威胁。这些平台通过传播假信息、影响政治选举和破坏欧洲团结，对欧洲的民主和文化构成风险。美国亿万富翁利用这些平台扩大其政治和经济影响力，例如埃隆·马斯克恢复被禁的极端账号。此外，美国平台通过法律如CLOUD Act获取欧洲用户数据，并通过税务漏洞剥削欧洲经济。文章呼吁欧洲建立自己的主权社交媒体生态，以保护数据隐私、促进文化多样性，并减少对美国平台的依赖。欧洲正面临数字主权危机，需采取行动应对。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：欧洲是否应建立自主的科技和社交媒体平台，以及全球化和主权对科技发展的影响。

不同观点：
• teekert：认为目前已有许多开源的免费平台，但用户更喜欢美国的广告支持平台，对开源替代品不感兴趣，尽管这对一些人来说很困扰。
• emigre：欧洲应发展自己的科技行业以与中国和美国竞争，但欧洲的碎片化使其难以聚集足够的资本和消费者来创建和壮大科技公司，未来是否有政治意愿改变这一点还有待观察。
• seydor：社交媒体实际上是个人广告服务，商业部分只是赚钱的工具。
• qwertox：提议建立一个所有用户都经过验证的社交网络，用户必须使用真实身份，以减少虚假信息和不良言论，非法内容会导致直接后果。
• nottorp：欧洲需要多个竞争的社交媒体平台，但目前的监管措施反而增加了进入壁垒，导致难以实现这一目标。
• ashvardanian：去中心化的社交媒体平台应有机会发展，但其最大的障碍可能是用户界面、应用可用性、用户体验和内容发现等方面的问题。
• thinkingemote：反全球化运动正在引发一种反应，使得主权变得更加重要，这种反应正在导致更少的全球合作，同时在全球环境方面产生一种讽刺性的改善。
• gizajob：认为如果20年前就有这样的思考会更有用。
• beloch：Facebook的算法曾导致罗兴亚大屠杀，Meta拒绝承担责任并反对监管。当前的国际形势使得更多人开始关注这些问题，现在是转向FOSS替代方案的好时机。
• skwee357：认为不需要更多的社交平台，因为它们使人们脱离现实并传播 propaganda。
• varjag：建议采用纳税人资助的公共电视模式，没有广告，更好地对齐激励机制。
• Helmut10001：个人使用的Mastodon服务器在法兰克福运行良好，推荐这种解决方案。
• banqjls：质疑文章中对美国操纵的指控，指出例子中的事件涉及英国、德国和法国的主体，并认为文章实际上是在倡导对非进步言论的审查。
• haunter：文章中将欧洲和欧盟混用，不清楚具体指代谁，如果是27个欧盟成员国，内部的问题（如匈牙利）可能更严重。
• pipes：认为保护民主完整性和文化多样性实际上是在为审查提供借口。

补充讨论：

43592454.article_content:
Europe needs its own social media platforms to safeguard sovereignty
March 26, 2025
Social media has emerged as the central nervous system of global communication, shaping politics, culture, and identity. Yet, Europe’s digital public square is not its own. Over 80% of the continent’s social media activity flows through platforms headquartered in the United States—Meta (Facebook, Instagram), Alphabet (YouTube), and X (Twitter)—creating a dependency that undermines Europe’s autonomy.
Recently, it has become increasingly clear that European companies urgently need to build Europe’s own sovereign social media ecosystem to counter disinformation, protect democratic integrity, preserve cultural diversity, and reclaim control from US corporate and geopolitical interests. Europe’s sovereignty in the 21st century is at stake.
The threat of US interference: Disinformation as a geopolitical weapon
The 2016 Brexit referendum exposed how US-based actors exploited European vulnerabilities. For example, Cambridge Analytica harvested data from 87 million Facebook users—including millions of Europeans—to micro-target voters with divisive ads. Leaked documents revealed campaigns designed to inflame anti-EU sentiment, demonstrating how US corporate tools can destabilize European unity.
Moreover, false narratives about voter fraud propagated by US politicians on Twitter and Facebook flooded European networks, bolstering extreme movements. In Germany, the “Querdenker” movement leveraged these claims to protest COVID-19 measures, while in other countries, several disinformation groups backed by US billionaires amplified baseless accusations about election rigging.
It is important to understand that US platforms optimize for engagement and their owners interests, not truth. During France’s 2022 presidential race, YouTube’s algorithm disproportionately recommended far-right candidate Éric Zemmour, boosting his visibility despite his marginal polling. Researchers found that 60% of French-language election content on YouTube contained misinformation, much of it algorithmically amplified.
US billionaire oligarchy problem
American billionaires, including tech billionaires, wield outsized influence over European discourse. Elon Musk’s acquisition of Twitter (rebranded as X) led to the reinstatement of 62,000 banned accounts, including extremists, far-right figures like Germany’s Nikolai Nerling, who had spread anti-vaccine conspiracies, persons who committed several serious crimes in Europe, and persons who promote illegal activities such as rape and dehumanization of others. Meanwhile, Meta’s content moderation policies routinely ignore EU directives; in 2023, the European Commission accused Meta of failing to curb disinformation campaigns. Recently, several disinformation campaigns linked to US billionaires attacked EU officials on social media platforms, spreading false narratives and encouraging committing crimes (e.g., murdering officials or overthrowing governments in the EU). It has become clear that these platforms operate as extensions of US corporate power and the new US administration, prioritizing profit and political gains over Europe’s stability and safety.
Data colonialism: US platforms exploit Europe
GDPR vs the US surveillance state
While the EU’s
General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)
enshrines privacy as a fundamental right, US platforms remain bound by laws like the
CLOUD Act
, which grants American authorities access to data stored anywhere in the world. In 2022, the European Data Protection Board fined Meta for transferring EU user data to US servers, citing risks of NSA surveillance. Despite the EU-US Data Privacy Framework, experts warn that European data remains vulnerable to US intelligence overreach.
Economic extraction
US platforms siphon billions from Europe’s digital economy. In 2022, Meta reported €4.3 billion in EU revenue but paid an effective tax rate of 8.5% through Irish loopholes—€2.5 billion less than standard EU corporate rates. Google and Apple similarly route profits through tax havens, depriving European governments of funds needed for tech innovation. This financial drain perpetuates Europe’s dependency, stifling homegrown competitors.
Erasing Europe’s diversity
US platforms homogenize culture by privileging English-language content aligning with the worldview of the current US presidential administration and US billionaires. More than 70% of trends on social media originate in the US, overshadowing local creators. European journalists and influencers struggle to compete with US influencers, while platforms like Instagram algorithmically promote American beauty standards, marginalizing Europe’s diverse cultural identities. The shrinking visibility of local users and their regional languages also threatens linguistic heritage of Europe.
Europe is facing digital sovereignty crisis

43592125.article_content:
iPhones Could Cost Up to $2,300 in the U.S. Due to Tariffs, Analyst Says
Friday April 4, 2025 9:30 am PDT
by
Joe Rossignol
U.S. President Donald Trump on Wednesday
announced
that steep tariffs will be applied to imports from many countries, starting April 9. The tariffs could have a significant impact on Apple, as the company assembles the majority of iPhones in China, and products imported to the U.S. from China will be subject to a 54% tariff.
iPhone prices could increase by up to 43% in the U.S. due to the tariffs, according to analysts at equity research firm Rosenblatt Securities (
via
Reuters
).
Based on that prediction, the top-of-the-line iPhone 16 Pro Max model with 1TB of storage could rise from $1,599 to nearly $2,300 in the U.S., should Apple actually follow through with raising prices by 43% to offset the cost of tariffs.
At the other end of the iPhone lineup, the most affordable iPhone 16e model would increase from $599 to just over $850 with a 43% price increase.
An iPhone 16 Pro with 256GB of storage could rise from $999 to more than $1,400.
Apple would need to raise its prices by at least 30% on average, in order to offset the tariffs, according to Counterpoint Research's Neil Shah.
Apple has yet to publicly comment on the tariffs, so it is unclear if the company will actually raise prices, or if it will get creative and
find alternative ways
to offset the impact. It is also unclear if iPhone 16 models would increase in price, or if Apple would simply set higher prices on iPhone 17 models from the get-go later this year.
Apple's stock price is
down nearly 15%
since Trump announced the planned tariffs.
Note: Due to the political or social nature of the discussion regarding this topic, the discussion thread is located in our
Political News
forum.  All forum members and site visitors are welcome to read and follow the thread, but posting is limited to forum members with at least 100 posts.

• 反对观点1：部分用户对BluOS系统提出批评，认为其用户界面不够直观，操作复杂。例如，有用户提到在使用过程中遇到菜单混乱和操作不便的问题，特别是在与其他系统（如Sonos）比较时，认为BluOS的用户体验较差。

• 支持观点2：有用户认为BluOS相对于Sonos等竞争对手有明显优势，尤其是在音质方面。他们指出BluOS支持MQA和更高的音频解析度，这对于追求高品质音频体验的用户来说非常重要。

• 反对观点2：反对者指出BluOS的硬件价格较高，认为性价比不如Sonos等竞争产品。他们认为虽然BluOS在音质上有一定优势，但对于普通用户来说，这种音质差异在日常使用中并不明显，不值得花费更高的价格。

• 中立观点：有用户持中立态度，认为BluOS和Sonos各有优劣。他们指出BluOS在音频质量和多房间控制方面有优势，但在用户界面和易用性方面不如Sonos。这些用户建议消费者根据自己的需求和预算选择适合的产品。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：BluOS系统用户界面的直观性和操作简便性是争议的焦点。支持者强调系统的功能强大和音质优势，而反对者则关注其复杂的操作和较高的价格。

• 其他讨论点：有用户提到BluOS的更新频率和售后服务，认为这些因素也是影响用户体验的重要方面。一些用户对BluOS的更新速度表示满意，认为这有助于系统稳定性和功能改进，但也有人提到在遇到问题时售后响应较慢。

• 额外论据：有用户提供了具体使用场景的例子，如在家庭聚会中使用BluOS进行多房间音频播放，认为其表现优异；而反对者则提到在日常简单使用中，Sonos等产品更为便捷。

总结：讨论主要围绕BluOS系统的功能、用户体验、价格以及与其他系统的比较展开，不同用户根据自身使用经验和需求提出了支持或反对的意见。争议的焦点集中在用户界面的直观性和操作简便性，以及系统的性价比。

主要讨论点：Ben Eater的 breadboard计算机教程的优缺点及改进建议

不同观点：
• rs186: 认为该项目耗时耗力耗财，不适合大多数人。具体指出：教程过时，设计有问题，部分部件难以获取，且最终产品性能低下。调试和寻找替代部件需要额外时间和精力，可能不适合没有数字电子基础的人。
• JKCalhoun: 支持Ben Eater的项目，认为其教程能有效帮助学习CPU工作原理，并推荐结合YouTube视频学习。个人通过该项目成功组装并运行了6502套件，认为该项目能带来成就感。
• nanolith: 认为Ben Eater的计算机是很好的起点，可以通过修改提升其性能，并能过渡到FPGA和HDL学习。分享了在hackerspace中通过扩展项目实现更强大功能的实例。
• brucehoult: 指出该计算机内存极小（仅16字节），功能有限，但确实是一个真正的冯·诺依曼架构计算机，适合理解基本概念。
• apricot: 认为Ben Eater的教程适合学习基础知识，但性能较低，推荐Gigatron作为更强大的替代方案。
• roland35: 分享了在大学期间类似项目的学习经历，认为这种项目非常有趣且具有教育意义。
• schoen: 建议考虑NAND到Tetris设计，该设计有更丰富的资源和生态系统支持。
• ata_aman: 支持Ben Eater的教程，认为其是理解基础构建块的优秀资源。
• Jun8: 建议跳过完整计算机项目，仅构建简单的时钟电路以降低入门难度，并提议对教程和部件进行现代化和扩展以提高项目吸引力。
• atum47: 高度评价Ben Eater的视频内容，认为其讲解清晰，是学习硬件的优秀资源。
• markus_zhang: 认为Ben Eater的视频内容质量高，值得推荐。
• codedokode: 提到"homebrew computer ring"项目，分享了更多DIY计算机的创意资源。
• giulianopz: 提到另一个DIY CPU项目，提供额外学习资源。
• asdefghyk: 建议使用wire wrap技术来简化布线过程，分享了个人在70-80年代使用wire wrap构建电路的经验。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于该项目的耗时、成本及最终性能是否值得投入，特别是对于初学者的学习曲线和挫败感。
• 多个评论者分享了通过扩展和修改Ben Eater项目实现更强大功能的实例，并提供了额外学习资源和项目建议。
• 改进教程和部件现代化是多个评论者共同提到的需求，部分评论者表示愿意为更现代化和功能更强的套件付费。

data.title: Compilers: Incrementally and Extensibly (2024)
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一门实践性的编译器课程，目标是构建一个将高级语言编译为x86-64机器码的编译器。课程使用OCaml开发，源语言为类似Pascal的Tiger语言。课程采用迭代、增量的方式开发编译器，逐步扩展源语言和编译器功能，每步都生成可运行、可测试的编译器。课程强调代码复用、可扩展效果以及对变量和属性的处理，采用tagless-final风格。内容涵盖词法分析、类型检查、优化、调用约定和汇编生成等。课程使用自定义构建工具build.ml，支持增量开发，并已在2022和2023年作为选修课讲授。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：编译器设计的教学和实践中的不同观点和资源推荐

不同观点：
• tiu认为当前的编译器教学材料缺乏对一些更深层次问题的讨论，例如AST结构设计、缓冲区与无上下文标记化/解析器设计、索引处理和错误同步、多代码生成架构支持、FFI处理、将编译器暴露为API等。他推荐了Carbon语言的设计以及一些相关资源，如dabaez的课程、Khoury学院的课程、Nora Sandler的书以及compilerbook.org。

• convivialdingo分享了自己在修改MIR c2mir JIT编译器以支持简单类和盒装字符串的过程中遇到的挑战，尤其是类型表示的困难。他认为中间编译器的存在是为了处理高度结构化的复杂性，并且这种复杂性会随时间变化。

• soegaard推荐了Abdulaziz Ghuloum的《An Incremental Approach to Compiler Construction》，认为这是非常值得推荐的资源。

• norir认为设计语言是编写编译器过程中最困难的部分，而大多数编译器课程过于关注实现细节。他反对一开始就针对x86架构，认为这是不必要的复杂性，分散了对语言设计的关注。

• Jtsummers推荐了Jeremy Siek的《Essentials of Compilation》，并分享了自己和非CS背景的同事一起学习该书的经验，认为这本书比其他教材更有效。

• codr7表示自己在发现Forth之前在编写自己的语言时没有取得多大进展，认为编写解析器是最不有趣的部分。

• djoldman描述了自己在学习和实践编译器相关内容时的挫折感，认为一种逐步扩展完整工作编译器的方法非常有吸引力，并引用了Ghuloum的方法。

• nate_martin批评了一些编译器实现课程选择使用OCaml等语言进行开发，认为这对学生来说增加了不必要的难度，因为学生不仅要学习编译器实现，还要学习一种新的编程语言。

补充讨论：
• 不同资源和方法的推荐反映了编译器设计社区的多样性和丰富经验。
• 争议的焦点之一是编译器课程是否应该一开始就针对特定硬件架构（如x86），以及是否应该使用某些特定编程语言进行教学。
• 类型表示和解析器编写被认为是编写编译器过程中的两个主要技术挑战。
• 逐步扩展工作编译器的方法被认为是一种有效的学习途径，可以减轻学习的挫败感。

Compilers: Incrementally and Extensibly
Introduction
Course Content
Build tool
Utilities
Free Variable as Effect, in Practice
a greatly simplified and abbreviated version, demonstrating the
incremental, feature-by-feature, step-by-step development of
interpreters and compilers in tagless-final style. The article
also explains using extensible effects in interpreting or compiling
code with variables. This technique is used in the present course.
Introduction
Compilers
is a practical course. Its goal is to build a real
compiler, which compiles a high-level language down to the actual
x86-64 machine code and produces an executable that runs on student's
laptops.  The source language is Tiger': a procedural language
in the spirit of Pascal -- or C with arbitrarily nested functions.
The compiler itself is to be developed in OCaml.
The other goal of the course is to give a taste of modern software
development, specifically: test-driven development, version control,
and the stress on reading, comprehending and extending code rather
than writing from scratch.
The characteristic of the course is an iterative, incremental
development: we start with the most trivial source language, develop
the full compiler for it, and then keep extending the source language
and the compiler in small steps, reusing the earlier work as much as
possible. At each iteration, we build a
complete
end-to-end
compiler producing runnable and testable executables, for a
(progressively larger) subset of the source language.
Another characteristic is the extensive use of tagless-final style,
taking the full advantage of extensibility afforded by
it. The extensibility here means
reuse
-- of type-checked and
compiled artifacts from the previous increment -- rather than copy-paste.
The compiler is hence structured as a stack of domain-specific
languages, with parsing at the bottom and assembly at the top. The
languages are extended by adding new operations here and there (and
only occasionally by redirection).
Yet another feature is the attention given to names, or
`variables', and associating attributes to them. Our approach, which
readily permits adding attributes at will and analyzing variable usage, may
remind some of algebraic effects.
We cover all standard material for the compiler course, from
parsing and type-checking to analyses,
optimizations, calling conventions and assembly generation -- but in a
quite non-traditional fashion.
This course was taught as an elective 15-lecture upper-level
undergraduate course in the Fall/Winter of 2022 and 2023.
Version
The current version is November 2024

Code for the section: Introduction to tagless-final style
Free Variable as Effect, in Practice
A greatly simplified version of the course, which still, hopefully, gives
the taste of the incremental,
step-wise compiler development. The article also explains
extensible effects in compilation -- the technique currently used in the course.
emulator.ml
[8K]
An elementary x86-64 emulator, to explain assembly in the
introduction. The knowledge of assembly is
not
a prerequisite.
Course Content
After the preliminaries and the introduction to tagless-final style,
we start on the developing compiler, from the simplest language
onward:
The simplest source language: only integer literals
Unary expressions, booleans, types
LL(1) parsing, lexing
Simple binary expressions
Migrating to
ocamllex
/
ocamlyacc
Local variables, scope
The meaning of free variables: environment or effect
Variable usage analysis and memory allocation
Full expression language
Dummy expression and sequencing
Mutable variables, assignment, function calls
Strings and string operations
Comparisons and conditionals
Loops
Function declarations, local functions and procedures
Type-checking, more formally and practically
Mutually-recursive functions
Nested functions
Final exercises
Build tool
The course uses a dedicated build system -- in a sense, a parred down,
specialized and tuned version of
make
. It is designed to support the
incremental, step-wise development and has only what is needed. It is
simple, fast, and portable across MacOS, Linux and WSL.
The build tool is actually an OCaml script called
build.ml
. Like
make
, the script accepts the list of
targets to make, and makes them in the given order, stopping in case
of error. The script is a regular OCaml file, and can be
edited as such: see the sample below. One should particularly note
compiler_manifest
, which lists all the source files needed to build the
compiler, and how to build them.
In 2022 the course used
make
. The experience showed why a custom
build tool would be more more pleasant and convenient to use.  First,
since our compiler is built by extending the earlier code, the source
code is spread through many steps (each in its own directory).  The
code on step23 may use the source code files in
step22/

data.title: A Vision for WebAssembly Support in Swift
data.author: LucidLynx
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Swift语言的未来发展方向，尤其是其跨平台编译、WebAssembly (WASM) 支持、Windows支持以及JIT编译等问题。

不同观点：
• isodev认为，Swift当前的工具在为Apple设备构建时已经处于勉强维持的状态，因此扩展到WebAssembly/WASI支持虽然可行，但不应牺牲其他急需的改进。他还指出，Rust和Go等语言已经有多年的WASM支持经验，而Swift要达到类似的水平还需要很长时间，且目前没有迫切的需求增加另一个WASM平台。

• zerr关注Swift对Windows的全面支持，尤其是包括所有必要库和工具链的支持，暗示当前的Windows支持不够完善。

• singularity2001希望Swift能在运行时支持接口类型，以便在没有大量胶水代码的情况下读取和写入WASM结构属性。

• WD-42质疑在2025年，除了Apple开发之外，是否有 compelling reason 使用Swift而不是Rust。

• turnsout对Swift持积极态度，认为Swift是一种令人愉快且高效的语言，支持WASM可以帮助其在Apple平台之外的开发中成为一个更合理的选择。

• nofunsir幽默地表达了对JVM支持的期待，尽管这并不是当前讨论的主要内容。

• troupo批评Swift语言的发展缺乏清晰的愿景，认为当前的做法使得编译器在处理简单的SwiftUI组件时也显得力不从心，且编译速度缓慢。

• cyberax则关注iOS上的JIT编译问题，认为当前的技术限制不合理，尤其是在Apple生态系统中。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是Swift是否应该扩展到WebAssembly支持，以及这是否会影响其他平台的改进。

• 也有对Swift编译性能和开发体验的批评，尤其是SwiftUI组件的处理速度和JIT编译的缺失。

这些观点反映了社区对Swift语言未来发展方向的不同期望和关注点，包括跨平台支持、编译性能以及特定技术特性（如WASM和JIT）的实现。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：跳跃蜘蛛（跳蛛）的特性、行为以及作为宠物的潜力

不同观点：
• 一些用户（如fipar和vharuck）认为跳跃蜘蛛可以被当作宠物，甚至像是朋友一样。他们提到跳跃蜘蛛会建造丝管作为藏身之处，主动狩猎，且行为有趣，能够与人类互动。vharuck还提到可以用手工喂食跳蛛，用棉签蘸糖水喂它们。

• 另一部分用户（如somishere和dev_l1x_be）则着重描述跳跃蜘蛛的外观和速度，认为它们的快速移动和美丽的色彩令人着迷。dev_l1x_be分享了自己在家中发现多个跳跃蜘蛛物种的经历，并表示这些蜘蛛无害且有趣，是生活的一部分。

• 有一些用户（如giantg2和nickpsecurity）分享了个人与跳跃蜘蛛互动的经历，描述了蜘蛛如何对环境做出反应，如追逐激光点或与人类进行“游戏”。nickpsecurity还提出了一个有趣的想法，即利用跳跃蜘蛛对抗其他不受欢迎的蜘蛛，尽管实际操作上可能不太可行。

补充讨论：
• 部分用户（如dreamcompiler和symbolicAGI）提到跳跃蜘蛛的独特视觉能力，指出它们拥有比大多数蜘蛛更好的视力，可以追踪猎物甚至与人类互动。

• 有些用户（如jillesvangurp和HankB99）提到了跳跃蜘蛛在文化作品中的形象，或分享了观赏跳跃蜘蛛的照片和视频链接，展现了跳跃蜘蛛的美丽和独特性。

• 争议焦点：虽然跳跃蜘蛛作为宠物的概念受到部分用户的喜爱，但对于害怕蜘蛛的用户（如codedokode）而言，跳跃蜘蛛仍然令人感到恐惧，即使它们不具备攻击性。

• 另外，有用户（如jtbayly和thenthenthen）对跳跃蜘蛛的基本生物学知识（如蜕皮现象）表现出新奇感，或者对技术问题（如页面重定向）表示了不满。

总体而言，讨论围绕跳跃蜘蛛的行为、外观、互动性及其作为宠物的潜力展开，展现了不同用户对这种生物的喜爱和敬畏。

data.title: Is Python Code Sensitive to CPU Caching? (2024)
data.author: leonry
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了Python代码是否对CPU缓存敏感。尽管Python是高级语言，无法像C++或Rust那样精细控制数据结构的内存布局，但实验表明，CPU缓存效应在Python中依然存在。作者通过顺序和随机访问列表元素的实验发现，随机访问明显较慢，尤其当数据大小超过CPU缓存时，随机访问速度会大幅下降。虽然Python的解释器开销大，但缓存效应依然显著。实验设计中考虑了多重指针访问对缓存的影响，结果显示缓存效应在Python中也不可忽视，特别是对于大型数据处理时。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：CPU缓存和分支预测在不同编程语言（尤其是高层次语言如Python）中的表现及其对性能的影响。

不同观点：
• PhilipRoman：提出CPU缓存效应在各种语言中都能观察到，但更关注解释型代码中是否能观察到分支预测效应。
• Delk：支持高层次语言如Python中存在缓存敏感性的观点，并通过Python列表的实现细节（如连续数组分配）解释了缓存友好的原因。同时指出，Python通过不同集合类型（如列表、字典、集合）来优化不同访问模式下的算法效率和缓存利用。
• PaulHoule：认同现代CPU的“机械同情”效应在像Python这样远离底层硬件的语言中也能感受到，强调缓存效应在这些语言中的显著性。
• SteelByte：赞赏文章对CPU缓存及其对Python性能影响的分析，并提出对其他动态语言（如JavaScript）的比较兴趣，尤其关注JIT编译器能否优化缓存低效问题。
• davvid：指出文章未提及Python的原子引用计数对缓存的不利影响，认为原子引用计数频繁失效缓存，对性能有负面作用。

补充讨论：
• Delk提到Python文档对随机访问效率的描述模糊，认为尽管文档未明确必须是常量时间随机访问，但实现上通常为缓存友好的连续数组。
• davvid的观点引入了对Python具体实现细节（如原子引用计数）对缓存负面影响的关注，与其他评论者对缓存友好的乐观态度形成对比，揭示了Python实现中可能存在的缓存利用问题。
• 争议焦点在于Python等高层次语言在实际应用中缓存效应的表现，部分评论者认为缓存效应显著且友好，而另一些人则指出具体实现细节可能导致缓存利用不佳的情况。

43555110.article_content:
Is Python Code Sensitive to CPU Caching?
2024-07-07
12 min
by Lukas Atkinson
Python (11)
Algorithms (3)
Cache-aware programming can make a huge performance difference,
especially when writing code in C++ or Rust.
Python is a much more high-level language,
and doesn't give us that level of control over memory layout of our data structures.
So does this mean that CPU caching effects aren't relevant in Python?
In this post, we'll conduct some basic experiments to answer this question,
by accessing list element either in sequental order or in a random order.
Results indicate that randomized access is consistently slower in Python.
Especially as soon as problem sizes outgrow the CPU cache sizes,
random access is multiple times slower.
Thus, some degree of cache-aware programming may be relevant in interpreted environments like CPython 3.12 as well.
Disclaimers:
Results may vary on different software and hardware.
The software used for these tests is CPython 3.12.
The CPU uses the x86-64 (amd64) architecture, Zen 2 microarchitecture.
This CPU generation had a fairly complex cache hierarchy
due to grouping cores in separate "core complexes" that partially share some of their cache.
Each core should see up to 32KB L1, 512KB L2, 16MB L3.
Background
Programs store data in memory (RAM), but this is slow.
CPU caches are faster, but much smaller.
The CPU has to decide which parts of the RAM to load into the caches.
Of course explicitly accessed memory addresses will be loaded into the cache.
But the act of loading data is comparatively slow, so the CPU will try to pre-load relevant data.
For example, we can expect the CPU to detect linear array access patterns
and automatically pre-load the next chunks of an array.
So
foreach
style loops over an array where all relevant data is directly inside the array
can be quite cache-friendly,
whereas random access cannot be predicted.
In practice, many arrays contain
pointers
instead.
We must dereference the pointer to a different memory location in order to get to the actual data.
Maybe the pointed-to location is already in the cache, maybe not and we will have to wait
– effectively also a kind of random access.
In Java (OpenJDK) and Python (CPython), all normal objects are actually represented as pointers to a more complex data structure.
In C notation, an array wouldn't contain
PyObject
values, but
PyObject*
pointers.
So clearly, Python data structures won't be as cache-friendly as data structures in C++ or Rust could be.
But Python already has a ton of interpreter overhead compared to natively compiled languages,
so maybe this doesn't matter?
In my experience, interpreter overhead tends to be in the 2× – 100× range, typically at least 10×,
and much worse if meaningful compiler optimizations are possible.
But typical values for the cost of accessing main memory vs L1 cached data also tend to be in the 100× range.
All of this is very rule-of-tumb, back-of-napkin,
but this suggests that interpreter overhead wouldn't drown out cache effects.
Designing an experiment
Our working hypothesis is: cache effects are detectable in Python programs.
This is not testable, so let's refine it based on the array iteration example above.
What we could try to observe is that the following program should take longer
when
indices = shuffled(range(len(values)))
("random" access)
than when elements are accessed in order (
indices = list(range(len(values)))
):
sum
(values[i]
for
i
in
indices)
But there are many different objects here at play:
indices
is an array containing pointers to integer objects
i
is effectively a pointer to such an integer object
values
is an array containing pointers to objects
values[i]
is effectively one such pointer
To drop to C notation for a moment, this means we have four different kinds of memory locations:
indices[…]
/
i
, which contains a pointer
*i
, which contains the actual index
values[*i]
, which contains a pointer
*values[*i]
, which contains the actual value
If we want to desing the experiment properly, we have to consider cache effects for all these memory locations.
The
indices
array is likely unproblematic as it will be iterated in order.
Each index
*i
however requires a memory access.
To reduce the impact of cache effects, it would be nice if these values are laid out sequentially in memory.
Python doesn't let us control that,
but in practice objects are likely to be allocated mostly one after the other.
So we want to create those integer objects in the order in which they will be referenced.
That means we must not shuffle indices within the Python process that runs the benchmark,
but can read in already-shuffled test data.
The
values
array is unproblematic, as it is the main cache effect that we want to test.
The
*values[*i]
elements may or may not matter.
Either the CPU is able to understand that
values
are actually pointers to values

43555110.article_summary: 本文探讨了Python代码是否对CPU缓存敏感。尽管Python是高级语言，无法像C++或Rust那样精细控制数据结构的内存布局，但实验表明，CPU缓存效应在Python中依然存在。作者通过顺序和随机访问列表元素的实验发现，随机访问明显较慢，尤其当数据大小超过CPU缓存时，随机访问速度会大幅下降。虽然Python的解释器开销大，但缓存效应依然显著。实验设计中考虑了多重指针访问对缓存的影响，结果显示缓存效应在Python中也不可忽视，特别是对于大型数据处理时。

• PhilipRoman：提出CPU缓存效应在各种语言中都能观察到，但更关注解释型代码中是否能观察到分支预测效应。

• PaulHoule：认同现代CPU的“机械同情”效应在像Python这样远离底层硬件的语言中也能感受到，强调缓存效应在这些语言中的显著性。

Multiplayer at the speed of light.
What is
SpacetimeDB
?
You can think of SpacetimeDB as both a database and server combined into one.
It is a relational database system that lets you upload your application logic directly into the database by way of fancy stored procedures called "modules."
Instead of deploying a web or game server that sits in between your clients and your database, your clients connect directly to the database and execute your application logic inside the database itself. You can write all of your permission and authorization logic right inside your module just as you would in a normal server.
This means that you can write your entire application in a single language, Rust, and deploy it as a single binary. No more microservices, no more containers, no more Kubernetes, no more Docker, no more VMs, no more DevOps, no more infrastructure, no more ops, no more servers.
SpacetimeDB application architecture
(elements in white are provided by SpacetimeDB)
It's actually similar to the idea of smart contracts, except that SpacetimeDB is a database, has nothing to do with blockchain, and is orders of magnitude faster than any smart contract system.
So fast, in fact, that the entire backend of our MMORPG
BitCraft Online
is just a SpacetimeDB module. We don't have any other servers or services running, which means that everything in the game, all of the chat messages, items, resources, terrain, and even the locations of the players are stored and processed by the database before being synchronized out to all of the clients in real-time.
SpacetimeDB is optimized for maximum speed and minimum latency rather than batch processing or OLAP workloads. It is designed to be used for real-time applications like games, chat, and collaboration tools.
This speed and latency is achieved by holding all of application state in memory, while persisting the data in a write-ahead-log (WAL) which is used to recover application state.
Installation
You can run SpacetimeDB as a standalone database server via the
spacetime
CLI tool.
Install instructions for supported platforms are outlined below.
The same install instructions can be found on our website at
https://spacetimedb.com/install
.
Install on macOS
Installing on macOS is as simple as running our install script. After that you can use the spacetime command to manage versions.
curl -sSf https://install.spacetimedb.com
|
sh
Install on Linux
Installing on Linux is as simple as running our install script. After that you can use the spacetime command to manage versions.
curl -sSf https://install.spacetimedb.com
|
sh
Install on Windows
Installing on Windows is as simple as pasting the above snippet into PowerShell. If you would like to use WSL instead, please follow the Linux install instructions.
iwr https:
//
windows.spacetimedb.com
-
useb
|
iex
Installing from Source
A quick note on installing from source: we recommend that you don't install from source unless there is a feature that is available in
master
that hasn't been released yet, otherwise follow the official installation instructions.
MacOS + Linux
Installing on macOS + Linux is pretty straightforward. First we are going to build all of the binaries that we need:
#
Install rustup, you can skip this step if you have cargo and the wasm32-unknown-unknown target already installed.
curl https://sh.rustup.rs -sSf
|
sh
#
Clone SpacetimeDB
git clone https://github.com/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB
#
Build and install the CLI
cd
SpacetimeDB
cargo build --locked --release -p spacetimedb-standalone -p spacetimedb-update -p spacetimedb-cli
#
Create directories
mkdir -p
~
/.local/bin
export
STDB_VERSION=
"
$(
./target/release/spacetimedb-cli --version
|
sed -n
'
s/.*spacetimedb tool version \([0-9.]*\);.*/\1/p
'
)
"
mkdir -p
~
/.local/share/spacetime/bin/
$STDB_VERSIO

data.title: The Universal Transverse Mercator (UTM) geographic coordinate system
data.author: brendanashworth
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了通用横轴墨卡托（UTM）坐标系统，这是一种用于在地球表面精确定位的地理坐标系统。UTM系统将地球分为60个纵向投影带，每个带再分为南北半球，使用米为单位，通过东西向和南北向的网格线精确定位。与经纬度系统不同，UTM是平面直角坐标系，不使用负值，每个分区的坐标原点位于分区外部，称为假原点。UTM系统适用于北纬84度至南纬80度之间，而极地地区则由通用极地立体投影（UPS）系统覆盖。掌握UTM系统是野外导航的重要技能，有助于在野外快速准确地定位和导航。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：UTM坐标系的网格设计及其在实际应用中的问题

不同观点：
• SiempreViernes认为UTM网格是完全正方形且尺寸相同（1000米 x 1000米），但由于地球周长并非1公里的整数倍，导致投影中会出现未覆盖的狭长地表区域。具体来说，东西方向误差较小（17米），但南北方向误差较大（超过800米）。这一观点关注的是UTM投影在地球表面覆盖上的精确性问题。

• driggs则关注UTM和MGRS（军事格网参考系统）在GIS软件和GPS设备中的应用问题，特别是MGRS的网格行标识符（row designators）。driggs认为这些行标识符是多余且具有误导性的，因为UTM的北向值已经涵盖了一个区域的Y维度。同时，由于未排除字母"N"和"S"，导致GIS软件和GPS设备在显示南北半球时会产生混淆。例如，美国大陆的一部分被错误地标记为"17S"（南部 hemisphere），而实际上应为"17N"（北部 hemisphere）。

补充讨论：
• SiempreViernes提出的UTM投影覆盖问题涉及地球几何形状与网格系统设计之间的矛盾，是地理信息系统中一个基础性的技术难题。
• driggs的评论则更侧重于实际应用中的标识符问题，指出MGRS设计中的缺陷及其对GIS软件和GPS设备用户的困扰。这一问题虽然看似细小，但在实际操作中会引发混淆和错误。
• 争议的焦点在于MGRS设计中的冗余和不一致性，特别是半球标识符的排除和使用问题，这直接影响了用户体验和数据准确性。

总结来看，讨论围绕UTM网格系统的设计精确性及其在实际应用中的标识问题，反映了理论设计与实际应用之间的矛盾。

Becoming
proficient with the Universal Transverse Mercator (UTM) coordinate system — that
is, learning to quickly and accurately calculate the UTM coordinates of a specific
location on a topographic quadrangle (for input into a GPS unit) or plot UTM coordinates
on a quadrangle (derived from a GPS unit) — is an essential wilderness skill.
Mastery of the UTM coordinate system
is considered one of the pinnacles of achievement
among seasoned wilderness
land navigators
.
Top
Introduction to the UTM
coordinate system
The Universal
Transverse Mercator coordinate system — or UTM, as it's commonly referred — is
a international locational reference system that depicts the Earth's three-dimensional
surface in a relatively-accurate, two-dimensional manner.
Global coverage of the Universal Transverse Mercator (UTM)
and Universal Polar Stereographic (UPS) coordinate systems.
(Graphic by Michael
A. Neiger)
The UTM coordinate system allows users to accurately
and unambiguously identify geographical locations anywhere on the Earth's surface
between the northern limits of North America (defined as 84 degrees north latitude)
and the southern limits of continent of Antarctica (defined as 80 degrees south
latitude).
The remaining north and south polar regions — those
areas above 84 degrees north latitude and below 80 degrees south latitude, respectively — are
not included in the UTM coordinate system due to extreme projection distortions
in the UTM grid as compared to the meridians of longitude.
Instead,
these two polar regions are covered by the Universal Polar Stereographic, or UPS,
coordinate system.
Universal Polar Stereographic
(UPS) coordinate system:
According to the UPS coordinate system, the Northern
Hemisphere's polar region extends from 84 degrees north latitude to the North
Pole, which is located at 0 degrees north latitude. This region is split in half,
with the Western Hemisphere creating Zone Y and the Eastern Hemisphere creating
Zone Z.
The Southern Hemisphere's polar region extends from
80 degrees south latitude to the South Pole, which is located at 0 degrees south
latitude. This region is split in half, with the Western Hemisphere creating Zone
A and the Eastern Hemisphere creating Zone B.
To provide
a small degree of overlap for those operating on the margins of both the UTM and
UPS coordinate systems, the UPS system overlaps the UTM system by an additional
30 minutes of latitude.
Unlike the
Latitude/Longitude
coordinate system
— or LAT/LON as it's often referred — which is a three-dimensional,
angular-based, spherical coordinate system relying on the degree, minute, and
second units of measure, the UTM coordinate system is a two-dimensional, plane-based,
rectangular coordinate system relying on the meter unit of measure.
The
grid for the UTM coordinate system consists of parallel-running vertical (easting)
lines and parallel-running horizontal (northing) lines, each of which is spaced
exactly 1,000 meters (1 kilometer or
klick
) apart, all of which combine
to form a map-wide grid of 1,000-meter squares.
The overall
arrangement of the UTM grid is based on the Cartesian coordinate system, which
is a rectangular, two-dimensional (plane) system in which the abscissa X (horizontal
east/west) axis is replaced by a northing grid line, and the ordinate Y (vertical
north/south) axis is replaced by an easting grid line.
In
addition, the coordinates are meter-based and positive — they do not include
negative values. Since the X-Y origin point, or zero point, for each zone lies
outside the zone, the origin points are called false origins, and the coordinates
themselves are often referred to as false coordinates.
The Cartesian coordinate system was developed by René Descartes in 1637.
Rene
Descartes
1596-1650.
(Photo courtesy of
Louvre Museum, Paris, France)
René Descartes
(1596-1650),
was
a celebrated French philosopher, mathematician, scientist, and writer. His Latin
name was Renatus Cartesius.
Known
as the father of modern, rationalistic philosophy, Descartes philosophy came
to be called Cartesianism. His accomplishments included inventing co-ordinate
or analytic geometry through the merging of algebra and geometry.

• driggs则关注UTM和MGRS（军事格网参考系统）在GIS软件和GPS设备中的应用问题，特别是MGRS的网格行标识符（row designators）。driggs认为这些行标识符是多余且具有误导性的，因为UTM的北向值已经涵盖了一个区域的Y维度。同时，由于未排除字母"N"和"S"，导致GIS软件和GPS设备在显示南北半球时会产生混淆。例如，美国大陆的一部分被错误地标记为"17S"（南部 hemisphere），而实际上应为"17N"（北部 hemisphere）。

补充讨论：
• SiempreViernes提出的UTM投影覆盖问题涉及地球几何形状与网格系统设计之间的矛盾，是地理信息系统中一个基础性的技术难题。
• driggs的评论则更侧重于实际应用中的标识符问题，指出MGRS设计中的缺陷及其对GIS软件和GPS设备用户的困扰。这一问题虽然看似细小，但在实际操作中会引发混淆和错误。
• 争议的焦点在于MGRS设计中的冗余和不一致性，特别是半球标识符的排除和使用问题，这直接影响了用户体验和数据准确性。

总结来看，讨论围绕UTM网格系统的设计精确性及其在实际应用中的标识问题，反映了理论设计与实际应用之间的矛盾。

data.title: Mammoth de-extinction is bad conservation
data.author: rntn
data.article_summary: Colossal Biosciences aims to revive the woolly mammoth and other extinct species using gene-editing technology. The company has made significant strides, such as generating stem cells for the Asian elephant and producing genetically modified mice with mammoth-like coats. Founder George Church claims these efforts could combat climate change by restoring Arctic grasslands and protecting endangered species like the Asian elephant. However, critics argue that "de-extincting" mammoths is misguided, suggesting it's more about human spectacle than conservation. Evidence supporting the ecological impact of reintroducing apex predators, like wolves in Yellowstone, has been inconsistent, and similar claims about elephants' role in ecosystems lack strong scientific backing. While elephants do disperse seeds and affect plant life, studies show other species also contribute significantly, casting doubt on the dramatic ecological benefits touted by Colossal.
